title: Route-qualified clearance and distribution-volume interpretation
claim: Distinguish systemic CL from apparent CL/F, and terminal Vz, steady-state distribution Vss and structural central Vc. This card covers linear time-invariant single-dose NCA and a separately qualified steady-state clearance branch; it does not identify all parameters from isolated extravascular data.
conditions: Choose the explicitly qualified branch; scientific scope and assumptions are specified in method_recipe.
required_inputs: Use the branch-specific input contract below; unknown inputs remain unknown.
limitations: Offline candidate pending source and operational review; no target-human facts, fitting or production use.
downstream_use: Plan an evidence-bounded method and identify blocked dependent outputs; ContextBuilder supplies project objective separately.

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Distinguish systemic CL from apparent CL/F, and terminal Vz, steady-state distribution Vss and structural central Vc. This card covers linear time-invariant single-dose NCA and a separately qualified steady-state clearance branch; it does not identify all parameters from isolated extravascular data.
method_recipe.input_contract: Require dose amount/unit, route and infusion duration where relevant; analyte/matrix/free-total basis; dose-relative time; observed/censored status; AUC integration and terminal-tail qualification. Vz additionally needs qualified lambda_z; single-dose Vss needs AUMCinf and correct input-time treatment. Absolute extravascular CL additionally requires independently qualified F or jointly informative data/model. Vc requires a specified structural model with informative observations, not an NCA volume label.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Establish single dose versus verified periodic steady state, linearity/time invariance and compatible dose/concentration basis. The isolated oral Phoenix model cannot estimate F. Known F resolves the CL/F scaling algebra, but does not by itself remove absorption/input time from oral MRT. More informative joint designs need their own identifiability assessment.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: Dose: mass; C: mass/volume; AUC: mass*time/volume; AUMC: mass*time^2/volume; lambda_z: 1/time; CL: volume/time; V: volume; F dimensionless in (0,1]. Keep absolute and per-body-mass quantities distinct. Use AUC0inf for qualified single-dose total exposure; AUC over one dosing interval tau for the separately established steady-state branch.
method_recipe.procedure: Check basis/route and endpoint eligibility first. Compute only qualified denominators. Label CL/F or Vz/F when F is unidentified. For single-dose IV infusion verify whether software MRT has already subtracted Tinf/2; do not correct twice. Record Vc as a model parameter with its parameterization; do not rename Vz or Vss as Vc.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: Single-dose IV: CL=Dose/AUC0inf; Vz=CL/lambda_z. Isolated extravascular data give CL/F=Dose/AUC0inf and Vz/F=(CL/F)/lambda_z. IV bolus MRT=AUMCinf/AUCinf; constant-rate IV infusion MRT=AUMCinf/AUCinf-Tinf/2; Vss=CL*MRT under these qualifications. Steady-state IV CLss=Dose_per_interval/AUC_tau (REF_003:IMG2073). Do not reuse the single-dose MRT formula for steady-state data. If F is independently qualified, CL=F*(CL/F), an algebraic conversion.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Tail uncertainty propagates into CL, Vz and especially moment-based Vss. A mean-profile quantity is not an individual-parameter distribution. Unknown F confounds absolute clearance/volume; known F does not establish absorption-time or structural identifiability. No CI or terminal quality threshold is generated without a justified estimation method.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: Reject dimension mismatches and double infusion correction. A missing or nonpositive qualified terminal slope blocks dependent Vz/tail moments. Terminal contamination, absorption-limited terminal phase and inadequate sampling require qualification rather than automatic physiological interpretation. For 0<F<1, using CL/F as CL overestimates CL, not underestimates it.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If the tail is unqualified, retain observed peak/timing and a clearly bounded finite AUC if otherwise supported; do not compute CL by substituting AUClast for AUCinf. Unknown F retains apparent CL/F. Missing absorption/input-time knowledge blocks oral-MRT-to-Vss even if F is known; unknown Vc remains unknown. This tail restriction concerns single-dose extrapolated quantities; separately qualified steady-state IV CLss may use a fully supported AUC_tau without estimating a terminal slope.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Report route, dose, AUC/window, basis, absolute/apparent status and eligible versus blocked parameters with reasons. These are conditional kinetic estimates, not human efficacy, validated transfer or proof that Vc=Vss=Vz. Operational gates are reviewer synthesis of source definitions.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: SYNTHETIC arithmetic only: single IV bolus 10 mg, qualified AUCinf=5 mg*h/L and AUMCinf=20 mg*h^2/L give CL=2 L/h, MRT=4 h and Vss=8 L. In a distinct oral case the same dose/AUC gives CL/F=2 L/h; independently supplied F=0.5 gives CL=1 L/h. Counterexample: unknown oral input time still blocks Vss; an AUClast of 5 with unknown tail does not establish CL=2.

claim_support.claim: REF_003:0003 and REF_003:0005 explicitly define CL and Vz as apparent parameters (CL/F, Vz/F) for extravascular models because F cannot be estimated from isolated data, supporting the distinction between systemic and apparent estimands.
claim_support.scope: NCA parameter definitions for extravascular vs IV routes.

claim_support.claim: REF_003:0004 states Vss is computed for IV Bolus and Infusion dosing only and is not computed for extravascular dosing because MRTINF includes Mean Input Time, supporting the restriction of Vss calculation to IV routes in this context.

ADD002:0130 and ADD002:0132 describe structural model parameters (central compartment volume V, concentration C, bioavailability F as a parameter) distinct from NCA labels, supporting the requirement for a specified structural model to define Vc.
REF_003:IMG2073 and REF_003:0005 define steady-state clearance (CLss) as Dose/AUC_tau, supporting the separate steady-state clearance branch.

title: Dimensionally consistent cross-species clearance scaling
claim: Prepare a qualified cross-species clearance scaling scenario. Separate empirical size scaling from evidence that elimination mechanisms and route/basis are comparable. A calculable scenario is not an established prediction for an unstudied target.
conditions: Choose the explicitly qualified branch; scientific scope and assumptions are specified in method_recipe.
required_inputs: Use the branch-specific input contract below; unknown inputs remain unknown.
limitations: Offline candidate pending source and operational review; no target-human facts, fitting or production use.
downstream_use: Plan an evidence-bounded method and identify blocked dependent outputs; ContextBuilder supplies project objective separately.

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Prepare a qualified cross-species clearance scaling scenario. Separate empirical size scaling from evidence that elimination mechanisms and route/basis are comparable. A calculable scenario is not an established prediction for an unstudied target.
method_recipe.input_contract: Require animal CL with absolute or per-kg units, corresponding body mass, intended human reference mass and an explicitly justified exponent/model. Record IV versus apparent clearance, analyte/matrix/free-total basis, dose range, elimination mechanism and source population. Vss and organ flow are conditional inputs only for methods that actually use them.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Review nonlinear, renal/nonrenal, transporter and binding contributions and route/formulation differences before transfer. SUP010 compares specific methods/data sets; its tested exponents and species counts are study choices, not universal rules. If mechanism qualification is absent, retain only a visibly unqualified sensitivity scenario with explicit assumptions.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: CL absolute: volume/time; CL per kg: volume/time/kg; body mass: kg; exponent b dimensionless. Normalize units and multiply per-kg animal CL by that animal mass before applying an absolute-clearance allometric equation. Divide predicted absolute human CL by human mass only when a per-kg output is requested.
method_recipe.procedure: Document the input basis; convert to absolute quantities; choose only an independently supplied model/exponent; calculate; check reverse normalization and dimensional consistency; then list unresolved biological-transfer assumptions. Do not select a default exponent merely because mechanistic inputs are missing.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: SUP010 Eq1: CL_h,absolute=CL_a,absolute*(BW_h/BW_a)^b. The body-mass ratio is dimensionless. Its separate liver-flow method uses absolute flows; source per-kg LBF values are multiplied by species body mass before forming that ratio. No exponent-rule or multiexponential formula is prescribed here.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Separate animal parameter uncertainty, exponent/model uncertainty and species-translation uncertainty. Explicit ranges can support deterministic sensitivity scenarios; probabilistic intervals require supported distributions and dependence. Do not impose lognormality or call an arbitrary range a confidence interval.

title: Experimental Unit Identification and Partial Evidence Qualification

When unit identity or pool membership is unknown, individual trajectories cannot be inferred, but provenance-qualified descriptive evidence may be retained.

Multiple measurements exist per subject or sample.
Provenance of pooled samples or individual assignments is partially or fully unknown.

Metadata linking measurements to subjects, samples, or pools.
Treatment assignment records (if available).
limitations: Cannot reconstruct unknown pool membership or individual assignments from aggregate data.
Assay validation metrics do not establish biological independence.
Source guidance is general laboratory methodology, not specific to PK pooling algorithms.

method_recipe.procedure: 1. Identify the independently assigned unit for this design and endpoint (animal, cage, litter, animal-part or animal-period). 2. Separately identify serial-observation subject, specimen, pool and technical repeats. 3. Determine which joins and denominators remain supported; do not treat subsamples as independent n. 4. With unresolved provenance, retain only the descriptive displays whose grouping and denominator remain known, and block unsupported subject trajectories or inference. 5. Use an analysis respecting the nesting/repeated measures when estimable.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: None. Conceptual framework.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: High uncertainty in inferential validity if unit assignment is ambiguous.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: If independent assignment units or pool membership are unknown, block the specific individual-level joins and inferential n that depend on them. Retain aggregate or descriptive displays only when their source, grouping, units and denominator remain interpretable; otherwise mark that output unavailable.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If independent assignment units or pool membership are unknown, block the specific individual-level joins and inferential n that depend on them. Retain aggregate or descriptive displays only when their source, grouping, units and denominator remain interpretable; otherwise mark that output unavailable.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Valid inferential n equals the number of independent experimental units. Subsamples may inform within-unit biological variation and/or measurement error but do not independently estimate between-unit variation or increase independent experimental-unit n.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic: 50 cells measured from 1 mouse. Experimental unit = mouse (n=1). The 50 measurements are subsamples. Reporting n=50 is pseudoreplication. Measurements from subsamples (e.g., cells from one animal) do not increase the inferential n; treating them as independent causes pseudoreplication.
Repeated measures on the same unit are correlated and should not be treated as separate experimental units.

example_is_synthetic: True. The example illustrates the concept of subsampling vs. independent units without using specific project data.

title: Direct Concentration-Effect Modeling (Emax/Sigmoidal)
claim: Direct effect models relate plasma concentration to response at a specific time point or steady state, assuming no significant hysteresis or delay. Two primary forms are used: Sigmoidal Emax for stimulatory effects and Inhibitory Emax for suppressive effects.
conditions: For a direct time-course model, assess whether material delay is absent. A separately qualified steady-state or endpoint exposure-response analysis may remain informative when time-course hysteresis exists.
Requires a defined baseline (E0) and maximum effect (Emax) or baseline response (E0) for inhibition.
Exposure basis, concentration matrix, response endpoint and time/window must be justified and aligned; the response endpoint need not have an assay matrix.

Justify response/exposure time or endpoint-window alignment. Material time-course delay requires a qualified delay model; it does not automatically prohibit a separately qualified steady-state/endpoint analysis.
required_inputs: Response endpoint definition (e.g., tail flick latency, behavioral score).
Baseline response (E0) in absence of drug.

For parameter estimation: data spanning a supported response range to estimate the Emax increment above E0. For prediction with fixed parameters: a qualified estimate of that increment. An inhibitory form requires its declared baseline and inhibition parameterization.
Concentration (C) at the time of response measurement.
Hill coefficient h is estimated when identifiable, or externally fixed with justification; h=1 is a declared model choice, not a missing-value default.
limitations: A direct model may be inadequate for a time-resolved dataset with material hysteresis; assess delayed, turnover, active-metabolite, tolerance or endpoint-timing explanations. Steady-state or separately qualified endpoint exposure-response analyses may still be informative.
Parameters (EC50, Emax, E0) are study-specific and not transferable between drugs or endpoints.
Biomarkers used as endpoints are not automatically valid surrogate endpoints for clinical efficacy unless empirically validated.
downstream_use: Used to estimate in vivo potency (EC50/IC50) and maximum effect magnitude to inform dose selection and translational scaling.

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Estimate a defined concentration-response relationship using a qualified direct time-course or separate steady-state/endpoint analysis; do not force a direct time-course model when material delay is present.
method_recipe.input_contract: 1. Define the response endpoint and its unit. 2. Determine the baseline response (E0) from vehicle/control data. 3. Specify the exposure analyte, matrix and free/total basis; define the response endpoint/unit independently; justify their linkage and time/window alignment. The response need not have an assay matrix. 4. Identify if the effect is stimulatory (increase) or inhibitory (decrease).
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Define endpoint, baseline, exposure basis and observation window. Evaluate the time course where available; absence of material delay can support a direct time-course model, while a separate steady-state or endpoint exposure-response analysis can remain informative even when time-course hysteresis exists. Do not presume biomarker clinical surrogacy.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: Source-case stimulatory sigmoidal Emax: E=E0+Emax*C^h/(EC50^h+C^h), where Emax is effect increment above E0 and the absolute plateau is E0+Emax. Source-case inhibitory form: E=E0*(1-C/(IC50+C)); this tends to zero for that model and is not the only inhibition form. E,E0,Emax have response units; C,EC50,IC50 have concentration units; h is dimensionless.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Plot response vs. concentration to check for hysteresis. 2. If direct, select the appropriate model form (stimulatory vs. inhibitory). 3. Fit the model to the data using non-linear regression. 4. Estimate EC50/IC50, Emax, and E0. 5. Validate model fit and parameter uncertainty.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: Source-case stimulatory sigmoidal Emax: E=E0+Emax*C^h/(EC50^h+C^h), where Emax is effect increment above E0 and the absolute plateau is E0+Emax. Source-case inhibitory form: E=E0*(1-C/(IC50+C)); this tends to zero for that model and is not the only inhibition form. E,E0,Emax have response units; C,EC50,IC50 have concentration units; h is dimensionless.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Parameter estimates are sensitive to the range of concentrations tested. Lack of data at low or high concentrations can lead to poor estimation of E0 or Emax. Model misspecification (e.g., using direct model for delayed effect) leads to biased EC50.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: With material hysteresis, do not force a direct time-course model; compare evidence-supported delay mechanisms. If the concentration range does not identify a plateau, report Emax/EC50 uncertainty or nonidentifiability rather than fixing Emax without independent justification.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: With material hysteresis, do not force a direct time-course model; compare evidence-supported delay mechanisms. If the concentration range does not identify a plateau, report Emax/EC50 uncertainty or nonidentifiability rather than fixing Emax without independent justification.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: For the stimulatory form, Emax is the maximal increment above E0; the absolute plateau is E0+Emax. EC50 is the concentration producing half of the Emax increment. For the inhibitory form, IC50 is the concentration producing 50% inhibition of E0. High Hill coefficient (h > 1) indicates steep concentration-response relationship.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic arithmetic only: E0=5 s and an absolute tail-flick ceiling of 15 s imply an Emax increment of 10 s. With h=1, EC50=10 ng/mL and C=10 ng/mL, E=5+10*10/(10+10)=10 s. One point illustrates the equation but cannot identify EC50 and h; fitting needs a response series over informative concentrations. Counterexample: One response point at one concentration cannot jointly identify EC50 and Hill coefficient.

claim_support.claim: Sigmoidal Emax model for stimulatory effects: E = E0 + (Emax * C^h) / (EC50^h + C^h).
claim_support.scope: Study-specific example for tail flick latency.

claim_support.claim: Inhibitory Emax model for suppressive effects: E = E0 * (1 - C / (IC50 + C)).
claim_support.scope: Study-specific example for heat response score.

claim_support.claim: A direct time-course relationship is one model choice; delayed/persistent responses can produce hysteresis while exposure-response analysis may remain informative.
Biomarkers are not valid surrogate endpoints unless empirically validated.

example_is_synthetic: The worked example uses hypothetical values for arithmetic illustration; it is not a measured compound dataset.

title: Modeling Delayed Concentration-Effect Relationships (Hysteresis)
claim: When plasma concentration (Cp) and effect (E) exhibit hysteresis (counter-clockwise or clockwise loops), the delay must be modeled explicitly. Common mechanisms include distributional delay to the effect site (effect compartment), indirect response/turnover kinetics, or active metabolite formation. The choice of model depends on the shape of the response-time profile and available data.
conditions: Plasma concentration data is available (measured or qualified model-derived prediction).
Effect data is available.
A temporal delay between Cp and E is observed (hysteresis).
Mechanism of delay is unknown or requires discrimination.
required_inputs: Plasma concentration-time data (Cp): either directly measured or derived from a qualified PK model anchored by sparse sampling (e.g., satellite PK + terminal sample).
Effect-time data (E).
Baseline effect (E0) if applicable.
Maximum effect (Emax) and potency (EC50) parameters (estimated or fixed).

For a parent/metabolite model: qualified parent and metabolite exposure information and the declared relative-potency parameter (estimated or independently fixed); distinguish measured from predicted exposures and report associated assumptions and uncertainty.
limitations: Hysteresis alone does not identify the specific biological mechanism (e.g., distribution vs. turnover).
Model selection requires comparing goodness-of-fit and residual diagnostics.
Parameters like ke0 are empirical and may not represent a true physiological rate constant if the mechanism is indirect.

Active-metabolite contribution needs qualified metabolite exposure and potency information; parent-only data do not by themselves establish that contribution. Predicted metabolite exposure must be independently justified and its uncertainty disclosed.
Predicted Cp(t) introduces model uncertainty that must be propagated or qualified; it is not equivalent to direct observation.
downstream_use: Used to refine PK/PD models for dose selection, predict time-course of effect, and interpret exposure-response relationships in translational studies.
retrieval_keywords: hysteresis effect compartment ke0 delayed response biophase turnover active metabolite relative potency parent drug concentration equivalent satellite PK

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Estimate the rate of delay (ke0) or turnover rates (kin/kout) and the concentration-effect relationship (Emax, EC50) to describe the time course of effect relative to plasma concentration.
method_recipe.input_contract: Requires paired Cp and E data over time. Cp may be directly measured or derived from a qualified PK model (e.g., population PK anchored by sparse samples). For metabolite models, requires Cp_parent and Cp_metabolite.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Applicable when exposure-response data suggest a temporal delay. Require informative PK/PD observations and a qualified exposure model sufficient for the stated question; a dense numerical prediction grid does not add experimental information. If Cp is predicted, declare model structure, anchoring data and uncertainty; retain unresolved mechanisms when the data do not discriminate.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: Effect-site source case: dCe_site/dt=ke0*(Cp-Ce_site); E=E0+Emax*Ce_site/(EC50+Ce_site). ke0 is 1/time; Cp and Ce_site are concentration; E and E0 are response units. Turnover is a separate conditional family: use GEN002:MATH01–MATH08 for the four verified input/loss inhibition/stimulation equations rather than the raw equations. Active-metabolite source case: C_equiv=Cd+Cm*Rel.Pot (EXTA003:MATH01); C_equiv is a potency-equivalent concentration, not automatically the effect-site state Ce_site.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Align Cp(t) and E(t) times and inspect for a delay. 2. Fit or assess a direct relationship as a comparator. 3. Where supported, evaluate effect-site delay with stated initial Ce_site and ke0 units. 4. Test turnover only with the verified GEN002 equations and response baseline; test metabolite contribution only when measured/qualified parent and metabolite data exist. 5. Compare predictive adequacy, residuals and identifiability, retaining mechanism uncertainty when alternatives are indistinguishable.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: Effect-site source case: dCe_site/dt=ke0*(Cp-Ce_site); E=E0+Emax*Ce_site/(EC50+Ce_site). ke0 is 1/time; Cp and Ce_site are concentration; E and E0 are response units. Turnover is a separate conditional family: use GEN002:MATH01–MATH08 for the four verified input/loss inhibition/stimulation equations rather than the raw equations. Active-metabolite source case: C_equiv=Cd+Cm*Rel.Pot (EXTA003:MATH01); C_equiv is a potency-equivalent concentration, not automatically the effect-site state Ce_site.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Model misspecification can lead to biased ke0 or kout estimates. Identifiability of ke0 vs. kout may be limited if Cp and E are not sampled densely enough. If Cp is model-derived, uncertainty in the PK model propagates to PD parameters.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: If no model fits well, consider tolerance, sensitization, or unmeasured covariates. If metabolite data is missing, do not assume metabolite contribution; report parent-only model with caveats.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If no model fits well, consider tolerance, sensitization, or unmeasured covariates. If metabolite data is missing, do not assume metabolite contribution; report parent-only model with caveats.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: ke0 is the fitted effect-site equilibration rate in the selected structural model; kout is a response-turnover loss constant if a turnover model is fitted. Relative fit may favor one structure for prediction, but does not itself identify a biological delay mechanism.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic arithmetic: Cp=10 ng/mL, Ce_site=2 ng/mL and ke0=0.5 h^-1 give dCe_site/dt=4 ng/mL/h. If E0=5, Emax=10 and EC50=2 ng/mL, the cited effect link gives E=10 response units at this instant. This only checks equations; model discrimination requires an observed time course and appropriate competing evidence. Counterexample: A better-fitting effect-site model does not prove distributional delay over turnover or metabolite alternatives.

claim_support.claim: Effect compartment model equation: dCe/dt = ke0 * (Cp - Ce).
Direct effect model equation: E = E0 + (Emax * Ce) / (EC50 + Ce).
Hysteresis is a diagnostic for delay, not proof of distribution delay; other mechanisms like turnover or metabolites must be considered.
The source-case parent/metabolite potency-equivalent concentration is Cd + Cm*Rel.Pot; it is not automatically the effect-compartment state.
claim_support.scope: Conditional source illustration requiring qualified relative potency and compatible concentration bases; not a universal active-metabolite formula.

claim_support.claim: Satellite PK models anchored by sparse samples can provide qualified Cp(t) drivers for PD modeling when direct sampling is infeasible.
claim_support.scope: Source illustration of a qualified input-driver construction; applicability must be established for the current design.

example_is_synthetic: The numerical values (ke0=0.5 h^-1) are illustrative. The structural equations are source-supported.

title: Indirect Response (Turnover) PK/PD Models
claim: Indirect response models represent drug modulation of response production or loss, with zero-order input and first-order loss in the cited basic models. The untreated stationary reference is R0=kin/kout; it need not equal the actual initial response R(0). An upstream receptor-mediated action can coexist with delayed downstream turnover.
conditions: Applicable when the drug mechanism involves inhibition or stimulation of the synthesis or degradation of a biomarker/response.
Requires a measurable response variable with a stable baseline (R_0) and a turnover process that can be characterized by first-order loss and zero-order production.
A direct or receptor-mediated initial action does not exclude a delayed downstream turnover response; apply this branch when the measured response can plausibly follow production/loss dynamics.

For prospective model discrimination, seek informative baseline, onset, response-extremum and recovery observations across relevant exposures where feasible. Missing phases may limit discrimination rather than make all descriptive or bounded analyses unusable.
required_inputs: Plasma drug concentration-time profile (C_p).
Response variable time-course data (R vs. t).
Baseline response value (R_0) or sufficient pre-dose data to estimate it.
Initial response state R(0) at the start of the observation window (may differ from R_0 if pre-dosed or non-stationary).
Mechanistic knowledge about whether input or loss is modulated, if available; otherwise candidate structures may be compared and mechanism left unresolved.
limitations: Source includes theoretical and simulation-based model exploration; it does not prove identifiability of all four models from sparse clinical data.
Assumes stationarity (constant k_in and k_out in absence of drug).
Does not specify target-drug specific parameter values; parameters must be estimated from data.
Hysteresis observed in data may be due to indirect turnover or other factors (e.g., distribution delay); model selection requires mechanistic justification.
Dose-dependent shifts in PD-Tmax are model-conditional signatures, not unique biological identifiers; do not infer mechanism solely from Tmax shifts.
downstream_use: Use to fit PK/PD data where there is a delay between peak plasma concentration and peak response, or where response persists after drug clearance. Select the specific model (I-IV) based on whether the drug inhibits/stimulates input or loss.
retrieval_keywords: indirect response turnover kin kout inhibition stimulation input loss PD-Tmax effect compartment

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Estimate parameters k_in, k_out, IC_50/EC_50, and E_max/S_max to describe the time-course of a response variable R governed by indirect mechanisms.
method_recipe.input_contract: Input: C_p(t) (plasma concentration), R(t) (observed response), t (time), R(0) (initial response state). Output: Estimated parameters and model fit.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Use mechanistic evidence where available to choose plausible input/loss modulation candidates; otherwise compare supported alternatives without requiring every candidate to be fitted. Informative onset and recovery sampling improves discrimination, while missing phases may leave some parameters or mechanisms unresolved.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window:
1. Baseline: R_0 = k_in / k_out (Units: Response units). k_in (Response units/time), k_out (1/time).
2. Model I (Inhibition of Input): dR/dt = k_in * I(t) - k_out * R, where I(t) = 1 - C_p / (C_p + IC_50).
3. Model II (Inhibition of Loss): dR/dt = k_in - k_out * I(t) * R, where I(t) = 1 - C_p / (C_p + IC_50).
4. Model III (Stimulation of Input): dR/dt = k_in * S(t) - k_out * R, where S(t) = 1 + (E_max * C_p) / (EC_50 + C_p).
5. Model IV (Stimulation of Loss): dR/dt = k_in - k_out * S(t) * R, where S(t) = 1 + (E_max * C_p) / (EC_50 + C_p).
Note: Inhibition factor I(t) ranges 0 to 1. Stimulation factor S(t) ranges 1 to (1+E_max).
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Define response, baseline and exposure/response time alignment. 2. Define the untreated stationary reference R0=kin/kout. Set R(0)=R0 only when actual treatment history and response state justify equilibrium; otherwise use a justified observed/estimated initial state. 3. Select supported candidates among the four GEN002 input/loss inhibition/stimulation ODEs. 4. Estimate identifiable parameters from observed time courses and compare fit, recovery and plausibility. 5. Retain competing mechanisms when available data do not discriminate.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization:
1. Baseline: R_0 = k_in / k_out (Units: Response units). k_in (Response units/time), k_out (1/time).
2. Model I (Inhibition of Input): dR/dt = k_in * I(t) - k_out * R, where I(t) = 1 - C_p / (C_p + IC_50).
3. Model II (Inhibition of Loss): dR/dt = k_in - k_out * I(t) * R, where I(t) = 1 - C_p / (C_p + IC_50).
4. Model III (Stimulation of Input): dR/dt = k_in * S(t) - k_out * R, where S(t) = 1 + (E_max * C_p) / (EC_50 + C_p).
5. Model IV (Stimulation of Loss): dR/dt = k_in - k_out * S(t) * R, where S(t) = 1 + (E_max * C_p) / (EC_50 + C_p).
Note: Inhibition factor I(t) ranges 0 to 1. Stimulation factor S(t) ranges 1 to (1+E_max).
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Parameter identifiability may be limited if the response does not return to baseline or if sampling is sparse. Model selection between I-IV may be ambiguous without strong mechanistic prior. Dose-dependent PD-Tmax shifts are model-conditional and do not uniquely identify the mechanism.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: If the model fails to fit, consider: 1. Direct effect models with effect compartment. 2. Non-stationary turnover. 3. Incorrect assumption of inhibition vs. stimulation. Do not force a fit if the mechanism is clearly direct.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If the model fails to fit, consider: 1. Direct effect models with effect compartment. 2. Non-stationary turnover. 3. Incorrect assumption of inhibition vs. stimulation. Do not force a fit if the mechanism is clearly direct.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: kin is baseline input in response units/time and kout is baseline first-order loss in 1/time. IC50 or EC50 is the concentration giving half the specified drug-modulation term. In S(t)=1+Emax*C/(EC50+C), dimensionless Emax is the maximal increment and the factor tends to 1+Emax. Good fit supports model adequacy for these data, not unique biological mechanism.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic Example: Drug X inhibits the production of Biomarker Y. Baseline Y_0 = 100 ng/mL. k_out = 0.1 h^-1. Therefore k_in = k_out * R_0 = 10 ng/mL/h. If C_p = IC_50, I(t) = 0.5. dR/dt = 10 * 0.5 - 0.1 * R. At R=100, dR/dt = 5 - 10 = -5 ng/mL/h. Response declines. Counterexample: An observed hysteresis loop alone cannot identify which of the four turnover mechanisms applies.

claim_support.claim: Baseline response R_0 is defined by the ratio of production to loss rates.
Model I describes inhibition of input (production).
Model II describes inhibition of loss.
Model III describes stimulation of input.
Model IV describes stimulation of loss.
Indirect response models are distinct from direct effect compartment models and explain hysteresis via turnover.
Dose-dependent PD-Tmax shifts are model-conditional signatures and do not uniquely identify the mechanism.

example_is_synthetic: True. The example uses arbitrary units and parameters to demonstrate the calculation logic, not real data.

title: Human Simulation Layers: Typical, Variability, Uncertainty, and Residual Error
claim: Human PK/PD simulations should distinguish a conditional typical fixed-effect trajectory, between-subject variability, parameter/model uncertainty, and observation residual error. A typical trajectory is not generally the population mean. The population distribution and observed-concentration range require the relevant variability and residual-error inputs; uncertainty reflects limited knowledge that may narrow with information, whereas population variability does not vanish merely by increasing sample size.
conditions: Applicable when simulating human PK/PD profiles for dose prediction or covariate analysis.

For population predictions, specify the applicable random-effect law and covariance structure. For typical or conditional individual trajectories, do not require population BSV merely to define an observation model. Do not assume independence or zero covariance without justification.
Source-specific variability distributions from preclinical or prior studies are not universal defaults for new targets.
Residual error models are required only when the estimand is the observed concentration range, not for latent population exposure distributions.
required_inputs: For a typical latent profile: model structure, fixed-effect parameter values, covariates, dose and time grid.
For population latent predictions: specified BSV law/covariance and target-population covariates.

For observed-value prediction: a qualified residual-error model conditional on the chosen latent trajectory; add BSV inputs when predicting across a population rather than a specified individual trajectory.
For parameter-uncertainty bands: joint parameter covariance/posterior or a prespecified sensitivity set.
For future population uncertainty: qualified joint distribution over relevant fixed effects AND variability parameters (and residual parameters for observed-value events).
limitations: Typical parameter estimates do not correspond to mean predictions; mean predictions require simulating BSV.
Uncertainty in fixed effects should be included if the goal is to assess probability of exposure thresholds or covariate importance.
PD model translation from animal to human introduces structural uncertainty often underestimated if only PK uncertainty is propagated.
Missing target-specific BSV prevents population spread simulation; output is limited to typical profile.
Missing residual error prevents observed-concentration predictive range; latent population simulation remains valid.
If BSV uncertainty is unknown, label that layer unpropagated; do not assume fixed omega for future population range predictions.
downstream_use: Used to generate population concentration-time profiles, evaluate dosing regimens, and quantify uncertainty in human dose predictions.
retrieval_keywords: typical individual population variability parameter uncertainty residual error BSV uncertainty latent observed

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Simulate prospective human PK/PD scenarios while distinguishing typical latent trajectory, latent population spread, observations conditional on a trajectory/population, and parameter/model uncertainty. Add BSV for population spread and residual noise for observation-scale outputs; neither is a universal requirement for every scenario.
method_recipe.input_contract: Declare the estimand first. Typical latent trajectory: fixed-effect estimates and stated covariates. Population latent spread: additionally a qualified joint BSV law and relevant target-population covariate distribution. Simulated observations: additionally a residual model on the observation scale, conditional on the chosen latent trajectory. Parameter-uncertainty intervals: a qualified joint covariance/posterior or resampling representation for the parameters propagated. Future-population observed ranges also account for uncertainty in BSV parameters; disclose unpropagated layers.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Use a model qualified to the extent possible for the stated prospective question, with its evidence and unresolved extrapolation limitations. Reassess suitability when changing purpose or population; do not imply target-human validation exists. Supply justified distributional assumptions only for the layers being simulated.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: Typical latent prediction: C_typ(t)=f(theta_typ,covariates,dose,t). Individual latent prediction: C_i(t)=f(theta_i,covariates_i,dose_i,t), where the mapping from theta_typ to theta_i and its joint distribution must be supplied for the population branch. Observed concentration: Y_ij=g(C_i(t_ij),epsilon_ij) only if a specified residual-error model is included. Population mean latent profile is E_i[C_i(t)] under the stated population distribution; a typical curve need not equal it. No Normal or lognormal law is implicit.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. State whether the question asks for typical latent exposure, population individual predictions, observed-value range, or parameter/model uncertainty. 2. Compute the typical trajectory from declared fixed effects and covariates. 3. Add BSV only with a supplied joint random-effects law and realistic covariate distribution. 4. Add residual error only when predicting observations. 5. Propagate fixed-effect uncertainty only from a qualified joint covariance/posterior or use explicitly labelled sensitivity scenarios. 6. For future population range predictions, propagate uncertainty in BSV parameters (omega) alongside fixed effects. 7. Report each layer separately before any combined analysis.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: Typical latent prediction: C_typ(t)=f(theta_typ,covariates,dose,t). Individual latent prediction: C_i(t)=f(theta_i,covariates_i,dose_i,t), where the mapping from theta_typ to theta_i and its joint distribution must be supplied for the population branch. Observed concentration: Y_ij=g(C_i(t_ij),epsilon_ij) only if a specified residual-error model is included. Population mean latent profile is E_i[C_i(t)] under the stated population distribution; a typical curve need not equal it. No Normal or lognormal law is implicit.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Uncertainty is epistemic (limited knowledge) and decreases with more data. Variability is aleatoric (system property) and does not decrease with sample size. Confusing these biases decision-making. Uncertainty in BSV parameters must be accounted for when predicting future population observed ranges.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: If BSV is unknown, retain the typical latent profile but do not report population percentiles. If parameter covariance/posterior is absent, do not turn marginal standard errors into a joint uncertainty band; use named one-at-a-time sensitivity scenarios if justified. If residual error is absent, do not claim an observed-concentration predictive range. If BSV uncertainty is unknown, label that layer unpropagated.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If BSV is unknown, retain the typical latent profile but do not report population percentiles. If parameter covariance/posterior is absent, do not turn marginal standard errors into a joint uncertainty band; use named one-at-a-time sensitivity scenarios if justified. If residual error is absent, do not claim an observed-concentration predictive range. If BSV uncertainty is unknown, label that layer unpropagated.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Typical profile: single curve representing the 'typical' individual. Population distribution: range of individual predictions. Uncertainty bands: intervals over parameter uncertainty (epistemic). Mean profile: average of many simulated individuals with BSV. Threshold probability: calculated separately from an explicit event/distribution.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic calculation only: for an IV bolus of 100 mg with CL=10 L/h and V=50 L, k=CL/V=0.2 h^-1, C_typ(0)=100/50=2 mg/L and C_typ(1 h)=2*exp(-0.2)=1.637 mg/L. Without a BSV law, this is not a population distribution. Without a joint parameter-uncertainty distribution, marginal CL/V standard errors alone do not create a defensible uncertainty band. Counterexample: Marginal CL and V standard errors without covariance do not define a joint uncertainty band.

claim_support.claim: Typical estimates do not correspond to mean predictions; mean predictions require simulating BSV.
Uncertainty represents limited knowledge and decreases with information; variability is a system property.
Correlation between random effects must be accounted for to avoid unrealistic parameter combinations.
PD model translation uncertainty is often underestimated if only PK uncertainty is propagated.
Residual error is added only when observed concentration range is the main interest; latent population simulation does not require it.
Uncertainty in BSV parameters must be accounted for when predicting future population observed ranges.

source_vs_engineering_conventions: Source-supported: Distinction between typical/mean profiles, definition of uncertainty vs. variability, need for covariance in BSV. Engineering convention: Host requires explicit distribution/covariance specification; default to reporting 'unknown' rather than assuming independence.
example_is_synthetic: The example uses hypothetical parameters to illustrate the distinction between typical profile with parameter uncertainty and a full population simulation. It does not represent real drug data.

title: Prospective Human Regimen Simulation, Sensitivity Analysis, and Parameter Provenance
claim: Prospective human regimen simulations require explicit specification of route, dose basis, administration schedule, and dosing interval. Sensitivity analysis must distinguish between deterministic parameter perturbation (e.g., worst-case ranges) and probabilistic uncertainty (e.g., Monte Carlo distributions). Oral bioavailability decomposition (Fa/Fg/Fh) is a conditional branch requiring specific IV/oral PK data and is not mandatory for all drugs. Exposure-only simulation outputs cannot establish safety, efficacy, or First-in-Human (FIH) doses without separate exposure-response validation. Model parameter provenance, including library model modifications and source justification, must be explicitly documented.
conditions: Applicable when simulating human PK profiles for new doses, regimens, or formulations.

Fa/Fg/Fh is an optional oral mechanistic branch when relevant oral and IV exposure, absorption information and consistent clearance/flow definitions support decomposition; otherwise use an explicitly uncertain oral F scenario without claiming its components.

Assess sensitivity for uncertain inputs material to the stated scenario; choose scientifically justified ranges and joint perturbations where parameters are correlated. PBPK CYP/transporter examples are conditional.
Applicable when using library models or virtual populations; modifications to these models must be identified and justified.
required_inputs: Route of administration (IV, oral, etc.).
Dose basis (mg/kg, absolute mg) and administration/infusion schedule.
Dosing interval and simulation time window.
Initial state assumptions (e.g., steady-state vs. single dose).
Exposure output metrics (Cmax, AUC, trough).
Parameter names, values, units, and sources (literature, estimation, or library default).
Documentation of any modifications to library models or system parameters.
limitations: Does not provide target-drug specific human PK/PD parameters.
Does not validate a specific biomarker or supply efficacy/safety data.
Original EXTA001 study data are not transferable to target drugs; use only as methodological context for Fa/Fg/Fh estimation.
Exposure-response relationships must be separately qualified; simulation alone does not prove therapeutic effect.
Does not automatically validate library model defaults; user must justify modifications.
downstream_use: Use to structure simulation inputs, define uncertainty propagation methods, and document parameter provenance. Use to justify parameter ranges and model modifications in regulatory submissions. Do not use to derive clinical dose recommendations without additional efficacy/safety evidence.
retrieval_keywords: human scenario design, dose regimen assumptions, PBPK sensitivity, uncertainty quantification, oral absorption modeling, parameter source justification, library model modifications, PBPK reporting

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Define the specific human PK scenario (route, dose, schedule) and the scope of uncertainty (parameter ranges vs. distributions). Document the provenance of all model parameters and any modifications to library models.
method_recipe.input_contract: 1. Specify route, dose, formulation, and schedule. 2. Define initial conditions and time grid. 3. Identify parameters for sensitivity analysis (e.g., clearance, volume, absorption rate). 4. List all drug-specific and system-specific parameters with their values, units, and sources. 5. Document any modifications to library models or virtual populations.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: If oral first-pass mechanisms are in scope, F=Fa*Fg*Fh may be considered with supported data and assumptions. EXTA001 used Fa=1 for its indirect Fg estimate as a study assumption; unknown Fa is an uncertainty/gap, not permission to set Fa=1. Library model modifications must be justified.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: Conditional oral decomposition: F=Fa*Fg*Fh (all dimensionless). In the original indirect method, metabolic/hepatic extraction and Fh depend on IV clearance, renal/biliary-route assumptions, liver blood flow and matched blood-versus-plasma clearance units; do not compute CLh/Qh from an unmatched total plasma CL. Concentration and exposure units must match scenario outputs.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Define route, formulation, dose basis, administration schedule, interval, time window, initial state and output metric. 2. Declare which human parameters are known, translated or scenario assumptions, including their sources. 3. Document any modifications to library models or system parameters. 4. Run named deterministic sensitivities using justified ranges; run probabilistic uncertainty only with supplied joint distributions. 5. For an oral first-pass question, estimate Fa/Fg/Fh only when the indirect-method measurements and assumptions are met, otherwise carry F as an uncertain scenario input. 6. Report exposure and uncertainty without inferring efficacy, safety or FIH dose.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: Conditional oral decomposition: F=Fa*Fg*Fh (all dimensionless). In the original indirect method, metabolic/hepatic extraction and Fh depend on IV clearance, renal/biliary-route assumptions, liver blood flow and matched blood-versus-plasma clearance units; do not compute CLh/Qh from an unmatched total plasma CL. Concentration and exposure units must match scenario outputs.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Specify ranges or joint distributions from source evidence, measured uncertainty or transparent scenarios. The 10-fold CYP and 30-fold transporter values in SUP016 are PBPK sensitivity examples, not default human parameter ranges; Normal, lognormal and log-uniform laws are not automatic.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: If IV data are missing, do not estimate Fg/Fh; flag oral absorption as a gap. If exposure-response is unknown, do not infer safety/efficacy from PK variability. If library model modifications are undocumented, flag as a reporting gap.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If IV data are missing, do not estimate Fg/Fh; flag oral absorption as a gap. If exposure-response is unknown, do not infer safety/efficacy from PK variability. If parameter sources are unclear, flag as a provenance gap.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Label each exposure result by its simulated layer: conditional profile, population variability, parameter/model uncertainty, or deterministic sensitivity. Exposure outputs alone do not establish efficacy. Without a qualified exposure-response link, retain the supported PK results and their limitations. Report parameter provenance and model modifications clearly.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic conditional arithmetic only: if hepatic blood clearance is justified as 10 L/h and hepatic blood flow as 90 L/h under the source assumptions, Eh=10/90=0.111 and Fh=0.889. Without measured oral systemic F and a qualified Fa, Fg cannot be solved. A 100 mg q24h oral scenario may still vary total F over declared sensitivity values, but yields prospective exposure scenarios only. Counterexample: An IV CL estimate without oral systemic F and qualified Fa cannot determine Fg.

claim_support.claim: Specify route, dose, formulation, and schedule for simulation.
EMA PBPK guidance recommends sensitivity analyses for uncertain, influential parameters using scientifically justified ranges and approaches; its CYP/transporter ranges are examples.

Monte Carlo can propagate the uncertainty components explicitly included in its joint input model; it does not automatically include unknown or omitted sources. One-at-a-time sensitivity plots answer a different, conditional perturbation question.
Exposure-response information supports dose/regimen adjustments but requires established relationships.
The original indirect intestinal-availability study uses F=Fa*Fg*Fh and assumes Fa=1 for its Fg estimate; unknown Fa is a limitation, not a default.
Fa uncertainty impacts Fg estimation; solubility/permeability limits affect absorption.

All system-specific and drug-specific components, as well as the sources of parameter values, should be clearly specified and justified. Modifications to library models must be identified and justified.
claim_support.scope: Parameter provenance and model modification reporting.

example_is_synthetic: True. The numerical values are illustrative only and do not represent any specific drug.

title: Target Attainment: Population Probability vs. Parameter Uncertainty
claim: A population PTA is the model-implied proportion of individuals meeting a defined target event under the stated population variability and scenario. Fixed-effect-only simulation gives a conditional typical attain/not-attain result, while parameter uncertainty concerns confidence in predicted attainment. Residual error is required only if the event is defined on future observed measurements rather than latent exposure. Uncertainty in BSV parameters should be accounted for when predicting the range of observed concentrations in a future population.
conditions: Applicable when evaluating if a dosing regimen achieves a specific exposure target (e.g., AUC > threshold, Cmin > MEC).
Requires a defined target event, direction (above/below), integration interval, and dose schedule.

A qualified PK/PD model and between-individual distribution are needed for population PTA; residual error is needed only for observation-scale events. Scientific/clinical qualification of the target is separately reported.
Without a between-individual distribution, report conditional typical attainment and, if supplied, propagated parameter uncertainty; do not label either a population PTA.
required_inputs: A qualified model for the stated scenario with parameter provenance; population PTA additionally requires a justified between-individual distribution. Its scientific qualification and remaining target-specific limitations must be stated.
Definition of the target event (e.g., Cmin > MEC, AUC/MIC > X).
Target cutoff value and direction (above/below).
Integration interval or time window for the target event.
Dose schedule and administration route.
Population demographic/covariate distributions (if covariate effects are included).
Joint distribution of fixed-effect parameters (for parameter uncertainty intervals).
Between-subject variability (BSV) estimates and correlations (for population PTA).
limitations: Does not provide universal target cutoffs; targets are project-specific.
PD model uncertainty is often higher and more project-specific than PK uncertainty.
Source guidance is nonbinding; does not validate specific biomarkers or supply target-drug data.
Does not specify a default random-effects distribution or residual error model; these must be selected based on model diagnostics.
Monte Carlo numerical error is distinct from model parameter uncertainty and must be reported separately if simulation size is limited.
downstream_use: Used to quantify the likelihood of achieving therapeutic or safety targets in a target population, informing dose selection and regimen optimization.
retrieval_keywords: PTA target event population probability versus parameter uncertainty BSV Monte Carlo error

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Calculate the proportion of simulated individuals in a target population who meet a specific exposure criterion (target event) over a defined interval. Distinguish this from the confidence interval of the typical individual's exposure. Separate model parameter uncertainty from Monte Carlo simulation error.
method_recipe.input_contract: Define the target event, direction, units, dose and time window. For latent-exposure population PTA provide a qualified PK model plus BSV/covariate joint distribution. For observation-scale attainment also provide a residual-error model. For parameter-uncertainty intervals provide a justified joint parameter distribution. Specify simulation size to assess Monte Carlo error.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Declare model qualification and extrapolation limits for the stated scenario. Population PTA needs a between-individual distribution. Without it, conditional typical attainment and supplied parameter uncertainty may still be reported, but are not population PTA. A defined target event is necessary for any attainment calculation.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: PTA = event-positive simulated individuals / total simulated individuals, a dimensionless probability reported as a fraction or percent. The event metric and cutoff retain their own matching units (e.g., mg/L or mg*h/L), basis and time window.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Define and label the target event, units, interval and population. 2. Simulate individual latent profiles under the supplied BSV/covariate law; add residual error only for an observed-value event. 3. Count event-positive individuals and divide by the full simulated denominator. 4. Separately propagate joint model-parameter uncertainty when available and report its effect on PTA. 5. State whether the target is externally qualified or a prospective hypothetical threshold. 6. Report Monte Carlo numerical error (e.g., standard error of the proportion) separately from parameter uncertainty.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: PTA = event-positive simulated individuals / total simulated individuals. PTA is dimensionless; metric/cutoff units and the event time window must match.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Parameter and PD-translation uncertainties should be considered when relevant; their magnitude is case-specific and cannot be asserted to dominate without evidence. Preserve known random-effect correlations. Distinguish between uncertainty in fixed effects (theta), uncertainty in BSV (Omega), and Monte Carlo simulation error.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: If BSV is unavailable, report conditional typical attainment with any justified parameter-uncertainty analysis, explicitly excluding population-probability claims. If the target is undefined, do not invent a cutoff; report the missing event specification. Distinguish a prospective hypothetical target from an externally qualified target.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If BSV is unavailable, report conditional typical attainment with any justified parameter-uncertainty analysis, explicitly excluding population-probability claims. If the target is undefined, do not invent a cutoff; report the missing event specification. Distinguish a prospective hypothetical target from an externally qualified target.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Report the defined target event, population/scenario and time window. Distinguish a typical-exposure parameter-uncertainty interval from a conditional population PTA estimate. For independent identically distributed simulated event indicators, Monte Carlo SE estimates conditional numerical sampling error; it does not represent parameter uncertainty. If theta/Omega uncertainty is propagated, report the across-parameter-draw PTA interval separately, together with target and model uncertainty assumptions.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic Example: A drug has a target of Cmin > 10 mg/L. A model with BSV on CL and V is used. 1000 individuals are simulated. 850 have Cmin > 10 mg/L. PTA = 0.85. This is distinct from the 95% CI of the typical Cmin, which reflects parameter uncertainty. Counterexample: A typical fixed-effect attain/not-attain outcome is not a population PTA.

claim_support.claim: Simulations based on fixed-effect estimates illustrate the typical individual, not mean predictions or population probability.
Between-subject variability is accounted for in simulations to show the range of individual predictions and calculate population attainment.
Uncertainty in parameter estimates is used to illustrate the probability of the typical subject's exposure reaching a cutoff or to evaluate covariate effects.
PD model uncertainty is often project-specific and can significantly impact dose predictions.
Exposure-response modeling helps understand relationships and optimize regimens but does not inherently establish causality.

source_vs_engineering_conventions: Source supports the distinction between fixed-effect simulations (typical) and BSV simulations (population). Engineering convention dictates defining the denominator and event clearly before simulation.
example_is_synthetic: The numerical values (10 mg/L, 850/1000) are illustrative placeholders to demonstrate the calculation logic, not real data.

title: Population PK Model Diagnostics: Convergence, Residuals, and Predictive Checks
claim: Assess fitted NLME models through separate numerical-convergence and precision checks, structural/practical identifiability questions, residual diagnostics with shrinkage caveats, simulation checks matched to the observed design, and independent-data prediction when available. Each diagnostic answers a limited question; none alone validates the model.
conditions: Applicable to nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) population PK/PD models.
pcVPC may be informative when VPC bins mix dose or influential covariate effects or when adaptive dosing impairs a standard VPC; choose and qualify the diagnostic for the model question.
External validation requires data not used for model building (model building vs. testing dataset split).
required_inputs: Final population PK model structure and parameter estimates.
Observed dataset with covariates, dosing history, and sampling times.
Censoring information (e.g., LLOQ/BQL status) for simulation-based checks.
Independent testing dataset (for external validation).
limitations: At substantial shrinkage (the guidance discusses roughly >20–30% SD-based shrinkage), EBE/IPRED/IWRES-based diagnostics can become less informative; interpret with caution alongside simulation-based checks.
Standard VPCs can be misleading under broad dose/covariate variation or adaptive dosing; pcVPC offers a prediction-corrected option, not an unconditional requirement.

The cited pcVPC paper uses matched omission of censored observed and simulated values, then checks censoring frequency by independent variable; this is a source-specific diagnostic strategy. Preserve BLQ flags and evaluate the chosen censoring approach for the analysis.

A condition number above about 1000 is a guidance diagnostic suggesting poor support for one or more estimates; scaling, parameterization, precision and design should be examined before any model change. It does not determine structural identifiability or a universal pass/fail.
External validation is limited by the scope of the independent dataset; it does not prove global identifiability.
downstream_use: Model qualification for regulatory submission or internal decision-making; identification of model misspecification; justification for model simplification or additional data collection.
retrieval_keywords: population PK model diagnostics convergence residual IWRES VPC pcVPC censoring external prediction

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Assess the adequacy of a fitted NLME model through numerical stability, residual behavior, and predictive performance.
method_recipe.input_contract: Requires fitted model object, observed data, and simulation settings (number of replicates, seed).
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Assess numerical convergence and fit failures first; a failed fit can still be diagnosed. Use VPC/pcVPC only with a suitable fitted model and a simulation design matching the observations and question. pcVPC is an option when prediction correction is justified. With high shrinkage, interpret EBE-based plots cautiously and supplement them with relevant simulation-based checks.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: Condition number: ratio of largest to smallest eigenvalue for the specified information/curvature matrix, with parameter scaling and matrix definition stated. Shrinkage: report software definition and estimate (e.g., SD-based EBE shrinkage relative to estimated random-effect SD); do not divide by an undefined “SD of population estimate.”
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Check minimization, numerical stability, precision and biological plausibility; treat condition number as a signal, not a verdict. 2. Assess residual trends and note shrinkage limits of EBE-based plots. 3. Simulate the fitted model under the observed dose, sampling, covariate and censoring design for VPC or a justified pcVPC; prediction correction is based on model predictions for each observation relative to a bin reference, not simply a median covariate. 4. If using the cited matched-omission pcVPC method for BLQ, also check predicted censoring frequency by the independent variable. 5. Test prespecified predictions on independent data if available and state the supported population/scenario.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: Condition number: ratio of largest to smallest eigenvalue for the specified information/curvature matrix, with parameter scaling and matrix definition stated. Shrinkage: report software definition and estimate (e.g., SD-based EBE shrinkage relative to estimated random-effect SD); do not divide by an undefined “SD of population estimate.”
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Parameter uncertainty estimated via bootstrap or asymptotic SEs. Standard VPC simulations from one fitted structure at fixed estimates reflect modeled interindividual and observation variation and replicated-study sampling variability. They do not by themselves propagate uncertainty about model structure. Parameter/model uncertainty requires additional justified sampling or structural scenarios.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: Investigate numerical failures, unstable parameters, misspecified variability or residual structure, and poor design coverage. High shrinkage reduces the weight of EBE diagnostics; it does not mandate ignoring all of them. A failed external check limits supported prediction in the tested setting, not every possible population.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: Investigate numerical failures, unstable parameters, misspecified variability or residual structure, and poor design coverage. High shrinkage reduces the weight of EBE diagnostics; it does not mandate ignoring all of them. A failed external check limits supported prediction in the tested setting, not every possible population.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Convergence: A low condition number is not evidence of convergence/precision by itself; report optimizer status, curvature scale, parameter precision, sensitivity and identifiability separately. Residuals: Absence of an obvious residual trend is compatible with, but does not establish, adequate fit; trends indicate misspecification. VPC/pcVPC: Name percentile levels, bins/strata, replicate count and matching observed/simulated statistics; compare each observed percentile to its corresponding replicate interval. Avoid a universal all-points-inside acceptance rule. External: Predictions should match independent observations.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic illustration: a fitted one-compartment model has condition number 500, CL EBE shrinkage 15%, and a pcVPC chosen because doses vary. These values alone do not establish acceptance. Review convergence/precision, residual and simulated percentile patterns, BLQ frequency if censored, and prediction on any independent cohort against a stated purpose. Counterexample: A condition number of 500 and shrinkage of 15% do not by themselves validate a model.

claim_support.claim: Substantial shrinkage can make EBE/IPRED/IWRES-based diagnostics less informative; the guidance gives a contextual roughly 20–30% SD-shrinkage range.
A condition number above about 1000 is a diagnostic indication of weak parameter support in the cited guidance, not a proof of global nonidentifiability.

pcVPC normalizes observed and simulated values using model predictions to address relevant within-bin prediction differences, including some dose/covariate and adaptive-design settings; it does not remove all variability or guarantee model adequacy.
The cited pcVPC method handles censored plotted values with matched observed/simulated omission plus a censoring-frequency check; it does not delete original data.
Identifiability is classified into structural (a priori) and deterministic types.

title: Antibacterial PK/PD Index Discrimination and Conditional Target Estimation
claim: Dose fractionation and fitted exposure–response comparisons can help discriminate antibacterial PK/PD indices. For an endpoint-count model, E0 is fitted untreated endpoint burden while B0 is bacterial burden when treatment begins; stasis solves the fitted endpoint at E=B0, and a 1-log kill solves E=B0−1. Any index ranking and target remain conditional on design, organism, infection site, endpoint window and supported exposure range.
conditions: For index discrimination, use dose fractionation or another informative exposure design that separates competing index predictions; declare which exposure features vary or are controlled. A prespecified-index target fit does not by itself independently rank indices.
For target estimation: Requires a prespecified index and matched exposure-response data; does not require independent ranking if the index is already established.
Target estimation is conditional on the specific strain, infection site, and achievable exposure range in the source study.
Applicable to antibacterial agents with concentration- or time-dependent killing.
required_inputs: Qualified unbound plasma concentration-time data, directly measured or estimated from total concentration with a justified fu and binding model.

MIC qualification: identify the pathogen strain/isolate and provenance, assay method/protocol and relevant medium/incubation conditions, concentration units, tested dilution range and any off-scale bound. Normalize compatible concentration units before calculating an index; verify comparability with the conditions under which the target was derived.
Bacterial burden (log10 CFU) at treatment initiation (B0) and at endpoint (e.g., 24h).
Dose levels and dosing intervals used in the study.
limitations: Source-specific numeric targets (e.g., specific AUC/MIC values) are examples only and must not be transferred to other drugs.
If the highest tolerated dose does not achieve the desired log-kill (e.g., 2-log), the target cannot be determined.

When unbound concentrations are derived from total measurements, use a justified binding relationship; concentration-dependent fu must be handled consistently. Direct qualified unbound measurements do not require a second conversion.
downstream_use: Used to define PK/PD targets for clinical dosing regimen design and to identify the primary driver of efficacy (AUC, Cmax, or Time>MIC).
retrieval_keywords: antibacterial PKPD index dose fractionation fAUC/MIC fCmax/MIC fT>MIC stasis E0 B0

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Identify the most predictive PK/PD index (discrimination) or estimate the exposure target (e.g., fAUC/MIC) required for stasis or specific log-kill (target estimation).
method_recipe.input_contract: Raw inputs: Qualified unbound plasma concentrations (directly measured or converted from total via fu), MIC, bacterial counts (CFU) at t=0 (B0) and t=end (E_obs). MIC qualification: identify the pathogen strain/isolate and provenance, assay method/protocol and relevant medium/incubation conditions, concentration units, tested dilution range and any off-scale bound. Normalize compatible concentration units before calculating an index; verify comparability with the conditions under which the target was derived. These are inputs needed before numerical index/target use, not outputs to infer from the fitted model.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Index discrimination requires an informative exposure design that separates competing indices; dose fractionation is one source-supported design. A prespecified-index target estimate needs qualified matched exposure, MIC and response data but does not require independent index ranking.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: Source endpoint-count example: E(X)=E0−Emax*X^gamma/(X^gamma+EC50^gamma), where E,E0,Emax and B0 are log10 CFU per sampled site, X is one chosen PK/PD index, gamma is dimensionless, and Emax is a positive maximal reduction. Stasis: E(X)=B0; k-log kill: E(X)=B0−k. If a study instead models change from baseline, transform both outcome and target consistently. fAUC/MIC has time units; fCmax/MIC is dimensionless; fT>MIC is time or percentage as declared.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Define site, organism, treatment-start B0, endpoint time/count and whether response is endpoint count or change. 2. Obtain qualified unbound exposure and MIC; derive each candidate index with its unit and window. 3. For discrimination: Use dose fractionation or another justified design that creates informative separation among indices. For target estimation: Fit the source-appropriate index–effect curve for the prespecified index. 4. Compare fit and predictive adequacy (for discrimination) or invert the fitted model (for target estimation). 5. Invert only an admissible fitted target (B0 or B0−k on endpoint-count scale) within estimated effect and exposure ranges; report uncertainty or not estimable otherwise.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: Source endpoint-count example: E(X)=E0−Emax*X^gamma/(X^gamma+EC50^gamma), where E,E0,Emax and B0 are log10 CFU per sampled site, X is one chosen PK/PD index, gamma is dimensionless, and Emax is a positive maximal reduction. Stasis: E(X)=B0; k-log kill: E(X)=B0−k. If a study instead models change from baseline, transform both outcome and target consistently. fAUC/MIC has time units; fCmax/MIC is dimensionless; fT>MIC is time or percentage as declared.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Parameter estimates (EC50, γ) have associated standard errors. R² indicates variance explained but does not prove causality. Extrapolation beyond observed doses is invalid.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: Poor fits across candidate indices warrant investigating model, endpoint, exposure and design adequacy; no universal R-squared cutoff is supplied. For the stated positive-Emax curve, delta=E0-(B0-k) must satisfy 0<delta<Emax for a finite positive interior inverse. Handle delta=0 as the zero-exposure boundary and delta=Emax as the asymptotic limit, subject to supported data range.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: For E(X)=E0-Emax*g(X) and desired endpoint B0-k, define delta=E0-(B0-k). A finite positive interior inverse requires 0<delta<Emax and the target to remain within fitted effect/exposure support. At boundaries or outside support report the appropriate boundary/not-estimable result; do not compare k alone with Emax. If exposure, baseline or endpoint data are insufficient, retain descriptive comparisons and explicit unresolved target status. If MIC units or assay/strain comparability remain unresolved, retain descriptive exposure-response observations and withhold a qualified numerical MIC-normalized index/target.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: A better-fitting index is the best-supported descriptor under the examined design, not necessarily a causal driver or transferable winner. E0 is the fitted untreated endpoint count; B0 is treatment-start count. A numerical target is conditional on strain/site/time/exposure and cannot be borrowed for the target drug.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic arithmetic: endpoint model E=7.5−3X/(X+50), with E and B0 in log10 CFU/site, X=fAUC/MIC in h. If B0=6.5, stasis E=6.5 occurs at X=25 h. One-log kill E=5.5 occurs at X=100 h. These values are only admissible if the fitted response and tested exposure range cover them; they are not target-drug values. Counterexample: For an endpoint-count model, stasis is E=B0, not E=0; an unreachable target has no inverse.

claim_support.claim: PK/PD index represents quantitative relationship between exposure and susceptibility; targets derived from nonclinical studies.
Sigmoidal Emax model used to fit PK/PD index to effect; E0 is effect in absence of drug; EC50 is index for 50% Emax; γ is Hill coefficient.
Index discrimination via R² comparison (e.g., AUC/MIC vs Cmax/MIC vs T>MIC).
Stasis value is defined as bacterial count at 0h (B0); model E0 is a fitted parameter.

The archived EUCAST reference specifies MIC concentration units and organism-dependent assay method/medium. Recording these with strain identity is a host data-qualification rule for compatible index calculation.
claim_support.scope: Conditional antibacterial use; no universal assay protocol or target transfer

source_vs_engineering_conventions: Source-supported: Use of sigmoidal Emax model, R² for index comparison, distinction of E0 from B0. Engineering: Specific software (WinNonlin) and unweighted regression are conventions from source but not universal requirements.
example_is_synthetic: The numerical values in the worked example are synthetic to demonstrate the algebraic inversion of the Emax model. They do not represent real data from the source studies.

title: MIC-Weighted Cumulative Fraction of Response (CFR) Calculation
claim: CFR is calculated as the sum of PTA values at each MIC dilution multiplied by the fractional weight of isolates at that MIC. Off-scale or missing MIC data must be explicitly tracked rather than renormalized. A CFR threshold (e.g., 90%) is a study-specific interpretation criterion, not a universal regulatory standard.
conditions: Applicable to antibacterial regimens when a qualified PK/PD target and PTA-by-MIC profile exist; the source study used fT>MIC because its studied agents had time-dependent killing.
Requires a defined MIC distribution (frequency of isolates per dilution).
Requires a PTA profile generated via Monte Carlo simulation or similar PK/PD modeling.
required_inputs: PTA profile: Probability of achieving PD target (e.g., 40% fT>MIC) at each MIC dilution.
MIC distribution: Count or fraction of isolates at each MIC dilution (e.g., 0.008 to 128 μg/mL).
Isolate denominator: Total number of isolates in the stratum used to calculate fractional weights.

MIC qualification: identify the pathogen strain/isolate and provenance, assay method/protocol and relevant medium/incubation conditions, concentration units, tested dilution range and any off-scale bound. Normalize compatible concentration units before calculating an index; verify comparability with the conditions under which the target was derived.

MIC dataset provenance: organism/isolate stratum, inclusion/selection rule, collection place and time (or explicitly unknown), source and aggregation/weighting scheme. Qualify representativeness for the intended population; a pooled reference distribution is not automatically a population resistance rate.
limitations: EUCAST ECOFF/TECOFF criteria govern distribution acceptance for cut-off setting, not CFR eligibility.
Source-specific CFR thresholds (e.g., 90%) do not constitute universal clinical reliability policy.
Truncated distributions (lower/upper end) must be handled explicitly; silent dropping of off-scale mass biases CFR.
