downstream_use: Used to assess the probability that a regimen will attain its PD index against a specific population of organisms, informing empiric therapy decisions.
retrieval_keywords: CFR MIC-weighted attainment PTA profile isolate denominator off-scale tails

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Calculate CFR as the weighted average of PTA across MIC bins. Scope is limited to the specific isolate population and MIC distribution provided.
method_recipe.input_contract: 1. PTA profile: Array of PTA values corresponding to MIC dilutions. 2. MIC distribution: Array of isolate counts or fractions per dilution. 3. Metadata: Total isolate count (denominator), off-scale counts, and missing data counts. 4. MIC qualification: identify the pathogen strain/isolate and provenance, assay method/protocol and relevant medium/incubation conditions, concentration units, tested dilution range and any off-scale bound. Normalize compatible concentration units before calculating an index; verify comparability with the conditions under which the target was derived. 5. MIC dataset provenance: organism/isolate stratum, inclusion/selection rule, collection place and time (or explicitly unknown), source and aggregation/weighting scheme. Qualify representativeness for the intended population; a pooled reference distribution is not automatically a population resistance rate. Qualify these before population-level CFR interpretation; PTA probabilities are supplied downstream model outputs, while MIC measurements and sampling metadata are source data.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Requires PTA for a declared antibacterial index/target at MIC bins and a compatible isolate distribution/stratum. The REF021 example used fT>MIC for its time-dependent agents; other appropriate indices remain conditional on evidence.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: CFR = Σ (PTA_i × w_i), where w_i = (Count_i / Total_Isolates). Units: PTA is probability (0-1), w_i is fraction (0-1), CFR is probability (0-1).
method_recipe.procedure: 0. Check MIC units, assay comparability and isolate-population provenance before combining bins; document any restriction of the estimand. 1. Align PTA values with MIC dilutions. 2. Calculate fractional weight (w_i) for each MIC bin using the total isolate count as denominator. 3. Multiply PTA_i by w_i for each bin. 4. Sum products to obtain CFR. 5. Explicitly report mass of off-scale, missing, or unmatched MIC data; do not renormalize weights to sum to 1 if mass is lost.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: CFR = Σ (PTA_i × w_i), where w_i = (Count_i / Total_Isolates). Units: PTA is probability (0-1), w_i is fraction (0-1), CFR is probability (0-1).
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Report MIC sampling and PTA/model uncertainty when estimable. The cited study used a Newcombe-Wilson procedure for its CFR intervals; choose any interval method according to the current weighted design and dependence structure rather than applying that procedure by default.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: If MIC distribution is truncated or incomplete, report partial CFR or withhold full CFR calculation rather than assuming missing isolates are wild-type or resistant. Do not silently renormalize weights.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If MIC distribution is truncated or incomplete, report partial CFR or withhold full CFR calculation rather than assuming missing isolates are wild-type or resistant. Do not silently renormalize weights. If assay comparability or intended-population representativeness is unresolved, a computable weighted result is only a labeled conditional/reference-distribution scenario; withhold a generalizable population CFR interpretation. Unknown metadata must remain unknown.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: CFR is the modeled MIC-distribution-weighted probability of attaining the specified PK/PD target in the declared isolate population and regimen. It does not alone establish clinical cure, reliable empiric coverage or a universal 90% decision threshold.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic mass-balanced example: among 100 total isolates, 45 have MIC 1 with PTA=0.9, 45 have MIC 2 with PTA=0.5, and 10 are off-scale with unknown PTA. The known weighted contribution is (45/100)*0.9+(45/100)*0.5=0.63. The off-scale weight is 0.10, so without further information full CFR lies between 0.63 and 0.73; do not renormalize the 90 known isolates. Counterexample: Known counts of 50+50 out of 100 cannot coexist with ten additional off-scale isolates in the same denominator.

claim_support.claim: CFR is the sum of MIC-bin PTA times a bin weight.
PTA is the proportion of trials achieving PD target at a given MIC.
EUCAST ECOFF/TECOFF criteria are for cut-off setting, not CFR eligibility.
MIC distributions are reference material and cannot be used to infer resistance rates directly.

MIC uses concentration units and organism-dependent reference methods/media; EUCAST pooled distributions combine locations, periods and selection schemes and cannot represent resistance rates. Provenance qualification before population CFR interpretation is a host rule derived from these limitations.
claim_support.scope: Conditional antibacterial CFR; no requirement to use a single universal assay

source_vs_engineering_conventions: Source-supported: CFR definition as sum of PTA × MIC frequency; use of Monte Carlo for PTA. Engineering convention: Explicit tracking of off-scale mass; prohibition of silent renormalization.
example_is_synthetic: The numerical values (100 isolates, specific MICs/PTAs) are synthetic for illustration. The method of weighting PTA by isolate fraction is source-supported.

title: In-Vitro Time-Kill Design and Regrowth Interpretation
claim: In-vitro time-kill assays require strict control of inoculum, drug stability, and sampling to distinguish true bacterial regrowth from drug depletion or assay artifacts. Regrowth alone does not prove genetic resistance.
conditions: Applicable to in-vitro bacterial culture systems with measurable viable counts.

Measure drug exposure or establish stability with a qualified assay/control when distinguishing drug depletion from biological regrowth; if unavailable, report mechanism as unresolved rather than excluding the time-kill curve.
Not applicable to in-vivo efficacy or clinical target attainment without further PK/PD integration.
required_inputs: Initial inoculum density (CFU/ml) and growth phase status (log vs. stationary).
Drug concentration design and actual exposure history with units; concentrations may be expressed relative to MIC, but the source 0.25–64x MIC range is not mandatory.
Actual viable-count sampling times and exposure schedule; ensure early kill and later regrowth can be seen where those are study questions.
Viable count method (e.g., plate count on blood agar) and Limit of Detection (LOD).
Control growth curves (no antibiotic) for each experiment day.

Measured concentration or a justified stability assessment is conditional on distinguishing drug loss from biological regrowth explanations. If absent, retain descriptive curves and label depletion unresolved; resistance versus persistence requires separate corroborating evidence.
limitations: Time-kill curves alone cannot distinguish all regrowth mechanisms (e.g., persister vs. resistant subpopulation) without additional molecular or single-cell data.
In-vitro results do not establish in-vivo efficacy or clinical breakpoints.
Drug degradation in broth can mimic bacterial regrowth if not measured.
Below-LOD values are censored data, not zero counts.
downstream_use: Input for PK/PD modeling (e.g., NONMEM) to estimate growth/killing rates, effect compartment delays, and heteroresistance parameters.
retrieval_keywords: time kill curve design, bacterial regrowth interpretation, drug depletion vs resistance, in vitro PK/PD input contract

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Estimate bacterial growth rate (ψ), killing rate, and regrowth dynamics under constant or degrading drug exposure. Scope is limited to in-vitro mechanistic characterization and design interpretation.
method_recipe.input_contract: Record experiment/run and replicate identities, inoculum, actual viable-count times and values, assay LOD/censor flags, intended dosing/exposure design and controls. Require measured exposure or justified stability evidence when assessing drug depletion; otherwise retain descriptive time-kill curves with depletion unresolved. Distinguish raw observations from parameters estimated by a later qualified dynamic model.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Use a qualified susceptibility assay and study-specific viable-count limit. Drug-stability information is important for interpreting regrowth but may be unavailable; in that case retain the curve and mechanism uncertainty.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: For an exponential phase with quantified positive counts, N(t)=N0*exp(psi*t), with psi in 1/time; doubling time ln(2)/psi is meaningful for psi>0. A negative psi denotes net decline and has a halving time ln(2)/abs(psi). Values below the count limit remain censored; the SUP006 LOD/2-first-value rule was study-specific, while ADD004 used likelihood handling. Neither is a universal imputation policy.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Establish organism, inoculum, control growth, drug exposure condition, sampling schedule and replicate lineage. 2. Measure viable counts and carry the limit/censor status through plots and analysis. 3. Where feasible measure drug concentration or run stability controls. 4. Compare early kill and regrowth against control and exposure history; consider depletion, adaptation/resting/persister and resistant-subpopulation explanations. 5. Choose a model only if the design identifies its parameters and retain mechanism ambiguity when data do not discriminate.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: For an exponential phase with quantified positive counts, N(t)=N0*exp(psi*t), with psi in 1/time; doubling time ln(2)/psi is meaningful for psi>0. A negative psi denotes net decline and has a halving time ln(2)/abs(psi). Values below the count limit remain censored; the SUP006 LOD/2-first-value rule was study-specific, while ADD004 used likelihood handling. Neither is a universal imputation policy.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Variability in starting inoculum growth phase (log vs. stationary) can affect initial killing rates. Consider a mixture model only if the growth-phase hypothesis is supported by data and identifiable; otherwise, use a justified simpler representation and retain uncertainty.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: If drug concentration/stability is unavailable, keep time-kill observations but label the regrowth mechanism unresolved; never assume stability. If counts are censored, retain limit flags and use a justified censoring method or report bounded conclusions rather than treating below-limit values as zero or applying LOD/2 by default.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If drug concentration/stability is unavailable, keep time-kill observations but label the regrowth mechanism unresolved; never assume stability. If counts are censored, retain limit flags and use a justified censoring method or report bounded conclusions rather than treating below-limit values as zero or applying LOD/2 by default.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Regrowth is an observation, not a uniquely identified mechanism. Exposure falling below a relevant activity range supports depletion as a possibility; exposure remaining high weakens simple depletion but does not prove genetic resistance or persistence. Confirmatory susceptibility, stability or mechanistic evidence is needed for stronger claims.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic interpretation: inoculum 10^6 CFU/mL; at 6 h the assay reports <10^3 CFU/mL, so reduction from baseline exceeds 3 log10 but the exact count is unknown. At 12 h a quantified 10^5 CFU/mL is regrowth relative to the 6 h bound. Measured drug at 12 h is 0.5x MIC, making depletion plausible, but not proving it or ruling out resistant/persister cells. Counterexample: A count <LOD cannot be replaced by an exact measured count, and regrowth with falling drug does not prove depletion is the only cause.

claim_support.claim: The source study measured drug concentration to assess degradation as one possible explanation for altered killing/regrowth.
Regrowth interpretation requires distinguishing drug depletion from biological resistance/persistence.
The source studies used different below-limit treatments (LOD/2-first-value or likelihood-based censoring); neither is a universal rule.
A source study used a mixture model to investigate inoculum growth-phase variation; it is not required for every time-kill dataset.

example_is_synthetic: The numerical values (10^6, 4x MIC, 0.5x MIC) are illustrative placeholders to demonstrate the logic of distinguishing depletion from resistance. They do not represent specific experimental data.

title: NCA Terminal Slope, Integration, and Sparse Design Protocol
claim: NCA integrates observed concentration-time data over a declared window using a stated interpolation and BLQ rule. A selected terminal log-linear regression is required only for lambda_z and extrapolation-dependent endpoints. Destructive/sparse designs use a mean-curve estimand and design-aware uncertainty rather than reconstructed individual profiles.
conditions: Concentration-time data and an explicit dosing/time origin are available for an observed-interval AUC; an individual serial profile and a destructive/sparse mean curve are different estimands.
A defensible terminal log-linear point set is needed only for lambda_z, half-life, AUCinf and endpoints depending on extrapolation; AUClast may remain eligible without it.
For sparse/destructive data, biological subjects and design-specific repeated sampling are identified before mean-curve uncertainty is assessed.
required_inputs: Observed concentration-time records with assay status and actual dose/time origin; declare whether the first postdose point is at dosing time or whether pre-first-sample input needs an assumption.
LLOQ and retained BLQ/censor flags, with a prespecified analysis-context-specific handling rule.
Sampling-design and subject/pool identifiers sufficient to distinguish serial from destructive/sparse mean curves.
Dose, route and F only if dose-normalized clearance/volume endpoints are additionally requested.
limitations: Do not impose universal adjusted-R2, point-count, or extrapolated-percent thresholds as pass/fail criteria; these are diagnostic aids.
NCA diagnostics do not imply a compartmental model or individual PK for sacrificial animals.
Phoenix software defaults (e.g., >=3 points for lambda-z) are implementation specifics, not universal scientific validity proofs.
downstream_use: Use to compute an eligible observed-window AUC, and conditional lambda_z/half-life/AUCinf when the terminal phase is supported; document integration, censor and sparse-design uncertainty. CL, Vz and MRT require separate route, dose, F, AUMC or infusion/input information and are not automatically produced by this bounded card.
retrieval_keywords: NCA terminal slope lambda_z estimation AUC integration linear log down sparse sampling destructive sampling mean curve

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Compute an observed concentration-time AUC on a declared interval; conditionally estimate terminal lambda_z, half-life and AUCinf. Keep individual serial and destructive/sparse mean-curve estimates separate. CL/Vz/MRT require further route, dose, F or AUMC inputs and are outside this bounded card.
method_recipe.input_contract: Require time origin, measured concentration/time/status, units, integration window and interpolation rule. Preserve LLOQ/BLQ provenance. For mean-curve NCA identify experimental units and repeated-sampling covariance design. Dose/route/F are conditional for derived CL or volume, not AUClast inputs.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Observed AUClast may be estimated without a terminal slope if the requested start/end interval is supported. Lambda_z and AUCinf require positive terminal concentrations, a justified log-linear region and compatible last observed or predicted concentration. Do not infer first-order elimination solely from a declining profile. Sparse SE handling follows the actual design and implementation.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: Lambda_z is the positive magnitude of an apparent terminal log-linear ln(C)-versus-time slope over a qualified terminal window, with units 1/time. In multicompartment kinetics or flip-flop absorption it need not equal a single elimination-process rate constant. AUC has concentration*time units; keep time and concentration units consistent (e.g., h and ng/mL).
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Declare dose time, measured times, units, serial versus sparse design, censor flags and target AUC window. Do not create a pre-first-measurement segment without a stated observation or rule. 2. Select terminal positive quantified points and regress ln(C) on t; lambda_z=-slope only when slope<0 and terminal region is credible. Record point IDs, interval, fit and residuals; Phoenix automatic >=3-point/adjusted-R2 rules are software choices, not scientific proof. 3. For each observed AUC segment choose and report interpolation. Linear trapezoid: Delta t*(C_i+C_{i+1})/2. In the cited PKNCA lin-up/log-down rule, use logarithmic interpolation only for a decreasing pair with both concentrations positive; use linear for increasing or decreasing-to-zero before Tlast; both-zero contributes zero. Its lin-log option is linear up to Tmax and log after Tmax only with positive endpoints, otherwise linear. BLQ is an assay status, not a measured zero: preserve it and justify any rule; never default to LLOQ/2 or deletion. 4. Sum from the declared start through Tlast. Conditional AUCinf=AUClast+Clast/lambda_z; identify observed versus terminal-regression-predicted Clast and report extrapolated fraction. 5. For destructive sampling integrate a mean curve without labeling it individual PK; assess uncertainty with the actual covariance/design. Phoenix omits sparse-AUC SE for log trapezoids in its implementation, not as a mathematical impossibility.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: lambda_z=-slope[ln(C) versus t] (>0 if supported). Linear segment AUC=Delta t*(C_i+C_{i+1})/2. For a decreasing quantified positive pair, log segment AUC=Delta t*(C_i-C_{i+1})/ln(C_i/C_{i+1}); equal positive values use the continuous limit C_i*Delta t. AUCinf=AUClast+Clast/lambda_z only with a qualified terminal segment; t_half=ln(2)/lambda_z; extrapolated%=100*(AUCinf-AUClast)/AUCinf. AUClast's start time must be declared.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Terminal-window choice, assay censoring, unobserved initial interval and tail extrapolation affect AUCinf. Sparse mean-curve AUC uncertainty depends on sampling design and covariance, not only per-time mean variances. Phoenix does not output its sparse-AUC SE with log trapezoids because that built-in linear-combination calculation does not apply; other justified estimators require separate verification.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: Inspect terminal point set, slope sign, fit residuals, sampling span and extrapolated fraction together. A nonnegative or unstable tail does not support positive lambda_z; retain AUClast if eligible. No universal p-value, adjusted-R2, >=3-point scientific proof or 30-40% extrapolation pass threshold is supplied. Missing dose-time or initial segment must be labeled, not silently assigned zero.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: Without a defensible terminal slope, report the supported observed-window AUC but not AUCinf/half-life. Without a justified dose-time to first-sample segment, report AUC from the first observed time or explicitly conditional AUC0-last, never silently relabel. Retain BLQ status. For sparse log-trapezoid AUC, do not invent a Phoenix SE; record unavailable/conditional uncertainty.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Report start/end window, interpolation and censor rules, AUClast with units, retained/excluded terminal points and lambda_z if eligible, Clast basis, conditional half-life/AUCinf/extrapolated fraction, and serial versus sparse estimand. Do not report CL, Vz or MRT without their separate route/dose/F/AUMC requirements.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic observed t=[0,1,2] h and C=[10,5,2.5] mg/L, with measured C at the stated start: linear AUC0-2=(10+5)/2+(5+2.5)/2=11.25 mg*h/L. With lambda_z=ln(2)/h, tail=2.5/ln(2)=3.60674 mg*h/L and linear-rule AUC0-inf=14.85674 mg*h/L. Under log-down for both positive falling pairs, AUC0-2=7.21348+3.60674=10.82021 and AUC0-inf=14.42695. If these same C values instead occur at t=[1,2,3], 11.25 is AUC1-3, not AUC0-last, absent a justified first-hour rule. A flat tail cannot supply lambda_z/AUCinf.

claim_support.claim: Lambda_z is the negative slope of a qualified ln(C)-versus-time terminal regression; Phoenix automatic selection and point-count rules are implementation details.
PKNCA distinguishes linear, lin-up/log-down and lin-log integration with explicit zero/end-point handling; BLQ handling changes the eligible profile.
Conditional AUCinf uses AUClast plus Clast/lambda_z, with observed or predicted Clast provenance.
Phoenix sparse NCA integrates the mean curve and omits its built-in AUC SE with log-trapezoid rules.
claim_support.scope: Phoenix sparse implementation, not all statistical methods

title: Candidate PK Model and Prospective Sampling-Design Assessment
claim: Prospective sampling assessment separates structural identifiability, local design-dependent parameter precision and candidate-model discrimination. A source-specific Jacobian/FIM approach can inform local precision under its assumptions; it does not establish global structural identifiability. Stochastic simulation/estimation (SSE) estimates discrimination for explicitly named generating and rival models under a specified design and selection rule.
conditions: Candidate models, target design and the prediction/precision question are named in advance; the generating structure and parameters in SSE are scenarios, not known truth for the target drug.
A residual/noise model and, for population SSE, a qualified random-effects/covariate model are specified or varied in sensitivity analysis.
FIM conclusions are local to the assumed parameterization/design; OFV likelihood-ratio cutoffs require suitable nested comparisons and stated degrees of freedom.
required_inputs: Explicitly named candidate structural PK models (e.g., 1-cp, 1-cp-lag, 2-cp, 2-cp-lag).
Parameterization scheme for each candidate (e.g., CL/F, V, Ka, ALAG, Q, Vp).
Residual error model specification (e.g., additive + proportional).
Candidate sampling schedules (time points, number of samples per subject).
Sample size (number of subjects) for design evaluation.
Assay limits (LLOQ/ULOQ) if censoring is relevant to the design.
Prior parameter estimates or assumed 'true' values for simulation.
limitations: No universal sample size, number of sampling points, or condition-number threshold guarantees model discrimination.
FIM-based precision is conditional on the assumed true parameters and design; it is not a universal certificate.
SSE results are specific to the simulated scenario and parameter values; they do not generalize to all drugs or conditions.
A local FIM/information test does not by itself establish global structural identifiability; any global claim needs a method suitable for the model and its assumptions.
The method does not replace model validation on real data; it is a prospective design tool.
downstream_use: Use to justify sampling schedules in protocol design, to estimate required sample sizes for model discrimination, or to assess the risk of model misspecification due to sparse sampling.
retrieval_keywords: PK model selection, sampling design, identifiability analysis, FIM, SSE, sparse sampling, model discrimination, population PK design

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Assess the ability of a candidate sampling design to (1) uniquely estimate parameters (deterministic identifiability) and (2) discriminate between competing structural models (model selection power).
method_recipe.input_contract: Specify candidate structural models and parameterizations; feasible sampling times/windows, subjects and samples per subject; assay limits and censor approach if relevant; plausible parameter/noise/random-effect scenarios; prespecified rival-pair/model-selection rule. Keep number of subjects distinct from number of simulated replicate datasets.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Applicable when candidate models and feasible designs can be simulated or locally evaluated with qualified assumptions. No named software is mandatory. Fixed-effects local FIM and mixed-effects population information are not interchangeable; assess the intended model and its likelihood appropriately.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: Structural identifiability concerns uniqueness of model parameters under ideal information; local FIM rank at one design/parameter point is not a global structural certificate. For the cited fixed-effects/noise assumptions, M_F=J^T Sigma^-1 J. Diagonal(M_F^-1) approximates parameter variances when regularity holds; SE_j=sqrt((M_F^-1)_jj). SSE success is the fraction of simulated replicate datasets in which the prespecified rule selects the generating model against a named rival.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Name structural candidates, target parameters and feasible design/sample-burden constraints. 2. Assess structural identifiability separately; examine local information for each candidate design under supplied parameter and noise assumptions. When invertible and appropriate, take sqrt(diagonal(M_F^-1)) to approximate SE, with scale and units. 3. For SSE, select one or more plausible generating models and parameter scenarios, simulate replicated datasets preserving the proposed design and observation/censor structure, fit the generating and rival models, and apply a prespecified pair-specific selection criterion. 4. Report fit failures, parameter precision, pair-specific selection frequency and simulation Monte Carlo error; repeat across plausible parameter/noise/design assumptions. 5. Keep design precision separate from model-discrimination probability.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: Under the cited fixed-effects assumptions only: M_F=J^T Sigma^-1 J; if invertible and regular, Var(theta_hat)_jj approx (M_F^-1)_jj and SE_j approx sqrt((M_F^-1)_jj). For SSE, success(pair,design)=number of replicate datasets selecting the generating model over the named rival / number of evaluable replicate datasets; report failed-fit count separately. Delta OFV=OFV_rival-OFV_generating is one source-study comparison, not a universal test. Chi-square thresholds such as 3.84 for 1 df apply only with justified nested likelihood-ratio conditions.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Uncertainty in SSE results arises from simulation noise; increase $N$ simulations to reduce Monte Carlo error. FIM precision is conditional on prior parameter estimates; sensitivity analysis on priors is recommended.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: A singular/ill-conditioned local information matrix flags local estimation/design issues but does not alone prove global structural nonidentifiability. Low SSE success limits discrimination under the simulated scenario; high pairwise OFV separation matters only under the prespecified rule and reliable fits. Inspect estimator failures and design/censor mismatch.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: When target-drug parameters are unknown, evaluate transparent plausible scenarios and state the unassessed range. If SSE is unavailable, report only local parameter-precision/sensitivity results from an applicable FIM; do not call them a proxy estimate of structural-model selection probability.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Report named generating/rival comparison, design, subjects and samples, number of simulation replicates/failed fits, pair-specific selection fraction with Monte Carlo uncertainty, and model-conditional parameter SE approximations where justified. No result is a universal sample-size threshold.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Source-case illustration only: SUP004 simulated a 2-cp-lag generating model against 2-cp no-lag, 1-cp-lag and 1-cp rivals across specified sparse schedules. For the five-point/20-subject design, the reported 96.40% success belongs to the 2-cp-lag versus 2-cp without-lag comparison under the source's selection rule; it is not a general design target. Toy precision calculation: if local M_F=diag(4,25) in compatible parameter units, diag(M_F^-1)=(0.25,0.04) are variances and SE=(0.5,0.2); these numbers say nothing by themselves about selecting a lag/no-lag structure.

claim_support.claim: Structural identifiability relates to the mathematical model structure and unique solutions, while deterministic identifiability relates to data informativeness and study design.
The Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) is constructed from the Jacobian of the model response and the residual variance-covariance matrix. Its invertibility and determinant assess identifiability.
A revised criterion for identifiability uses the relationship between the FIM determinant and random noise, avoiding numerical issues with zero determinants.
The diagonal elements of the inverse FIM assess parameter precision for a candidate design, reflecting deterministic identifiability.
Stochastic Simulation and Estimation (SSE) evaluates design efficiency by simulating data under a true model and fitting candidate models to calculate success rates (power) of model selection.
Model discrimination power depends on sample size and number of sampling points; sparse designs may fail to distinguish complex models (e.g., 2-cp-lag vs 2-cp).
In the source design, sampling across absorption, distribution and elimination phases provided informative observations for model discrimination; adequacy depends on the candidate models and design.
claim_support.scope: Source-study sampling strategy, not a guarantee

source_vs_engineering_conventions: Scientific statements linked to originals; synthetic arithmetic and host review safeguards are explicitly distinguished from source-study results.

title: Conditional depletion-to-CLint scaling and blood/plasma basis
claim: SUP012's well-stirred hepatic blood-clearance calculation uses physiologically scaled CLint and, when that CLint still includes incubation binding, the factor fu,B/fu,inc. An already unbound-corrected scaled CLint must not be divided by fu,inc again. The assay-specific depletion-to-CLint conversion remains a separate source gap.
conditions: Conditional hepatic IVIVE: a qualified assay-specific in-vitro CLint estimate, physiological scaling to the target species, QH, and binding terms on declared bases are available before numerical prediction.
If CLint is already corrected to unbound incubation concentration, do not apply fu,inc a second time; retain the applicable fu,B term.
Blood/plasma ratio is needed only when converting or comparing blood and plasma clearance/concentration bases; it cannot replace fu,B.
required_inputs: Assay-specific turnover data and verified conversion to in-vitro CLint with original units; this conversion is a SOURCE_GAP in SUP012 if not supplied elsewhere.
Physiological scaling factor(s) for the assay system and liver/body basis to produce scaled CLint in volume/time.
Liver blood flow QH in volume/time on the same species/body basis.
Qualified fu,B; fu,inc only if scaled CLint still includes incubation binding and needs that correction.
A documented blood/plasma ratio and measured-clearance provenance only if a blood/plasma conversion or prediction comparison is requested.
limitations: The indexed source (SUP012) demonstrates the well-stirred equation and scaling concept but does not provide a universal depletion-slope-to-CLint formula or specific numerical scaling factors; these must be sourced separately.
Low-turnover compounds may have high uncertainty due to experimental limits (e.g., enzyme activity decline in microsomes >1h, viability decline in hepatocytes >4-6h).
Does not model uptake, biliary secretion, or extrahepatic metabolism explicitly.
Blood and plasma concentrations/binding are distinct; do not equate them without documented conversion.
downstream_use: Use as a conditional hepatic blood-clearance scenario when assay-specific CLint, physiological scale, binding and QH inputs are qualified. Track uncertainty and blood/plasma basis; do not treat CLH alone as systemic CL, an observed human outcome or a dose recommendation.
retrieval_keywords: hepatic IVIVE well-stirred model intrinsic clearance blood plasma binding physiological scaling clearance prediction

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Predict hepatic blood clearance (CL_H) from in-vitro intrinsic clearance (CL_int) using the well-stirred model, accounting for blood/plasma binding differences.
method_recipe.input_contract: Record assay system, depletion/turnover and CLint derivation, units, target species, scaling factors and resulting scaled CLint (volume/time); QH on the same basis; fu,B and whether fu,inc has already been applied. Add blood/plasma ratio only for a cross-basis comparison. The exact generic depletion-slope equation and numerical factors are not supplied by SUP012.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: The source-supported well-stirred equation is an available conditional method definition. A target-drug numeric CLH prediction requires a verified assay-specific in-vitro CLint calculation, physiological scaling and declared binding basis; stop the numerical branch at any missing step without discarding the method card.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: In-vitro CLint: assay-specific volume/time per protein mass or cell amount. Scaled CLint entering the equation: volume/time on the same body/species basis as QH. fu,B and fu,inc are dimensionless fractions unbound in blood and incubation. QH and predicted hepatic blood CLH have volume/time units. Blood/plasma ratio is a separate basis-conversion input when justified.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Preserve the observed assay turnover and verify its protocol-specific conversion to in-vitro CLint (source gap here). 2. Scale with documented protein/hepatocyte content and liver/body factors to CLint in volume/time. 3. Declare whether scaled CLint is incubation-bound or already unbound-corrected. If bound-basis, apply SUP012's fu,B/fu,inc factor once; if already unbound-corrected, use fu,B*scaled_CLint,u without another fu,inc division. 4. With QH on the same species/body basis, calculate CLH=QH*X/(QH+X), where X is the appropriate binding-corrected scaled CLint. 5. Compare only with observed hepatic blood CL or an explicitly converted/partitioned quantity; do not equate total plasma CL with hepatic blood CL.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: SUP012 bound-incubation basis: X=(fu,B/fu,inc)*scaled_CLint; CLH=QH*X/(QH+X). If scaled_CLint,u has already been corrected for fu,inc, X=fu,B*scaled_CLint,u instead. QH, X and CLH all volume/time on matched species/body basis.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Uncertainty arises from in-vitro variability, scaling factor variability, and model assumptions (well-stirred). Low-turnover compounds have higher uncertainty. Identifiability of CL_int depends on accurate turnover measurement.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: Stop only the numerical prediction when the assay-specific depletion-to-CLint equation, scaling factor, QH or required binding basis is unverified. Inspect low-turnover detectability and blood/plasma basis. Do not infer that fu,B is supplied by a B/P ratio alone.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If depletion-to-CLint conversion or physiological scale is absent, report method and explicit gap without a numeric CLH. If fu,B is missing, do not substitute B/P. If observed comparison is plasma total CL, require matched B/P and hepatic-versus-total clearance provenance before judging accuracy.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: When inputs are qualified, output predicted hepatic blood CLH and a units/binding-basis ledger. Any comparison to observed clearance must match blood/plasma and hepatic-versus-total basis; otherwise report prediction without validation claim.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic bound-basis example: scaled CLint=10 L/h, QH=90 L/h, fu,B=0.1, fu,inc=0.5. X=(0.1/0.5)*10=2 L/h and CLH=90*2/(90+2)=1.95652 L/h. Equivalent already-unbound scaled CLint,u=20 L/h gives X=0.1*20=2 L/h. Wrongly dividing that 20 by fu,inc again gives X=4 L/h and CLH=3.82979 L/h; that is a double correction, not a new biological estimate.

claim_support.claim: For SUP012's incubation-bound CLint basis, the well-stirred equation uses fu,B/fu,inc: fraction unbound in blood divided by fraction unbound in incubation, not a blood/plasma binding ratio.
In-vitro CL_int is scaled to in-vivo CL_int using physiological factors.
Low-turnover compounds have high uncertainty due to experimental limits.

title: Residual Observation Error Scales and Phoenix Combined-Error Parameterizations
claim: An observation model links a latent PK/PD prediction to a measured value on a declared scale. Additive, proportional normal and log-additive errors have different conditional SD/variance laws. Phoenix's Mix Ratio and Add+Mult combined-error options use distinct sigma definitions and variance functions; neither supplies a universal residual default.
conditions: Applicable when fitting or simulating observed values; residual error is not mandatory for latent concentration/exposure scenarios.
Choose the error law and estimation scale using assay/error behavior and diagnostic evidence; Phoenix PK/PD menu preferences are examples, not general rules.
Phoenix log-additive transforms observations and predictions into log space only under its documented engine conditions, and requires positive inputs for that transformation.
required_inputs: Observed values, latent model predictions and their units/matrix/endpoint, with assay status including censoring limits.
A candidate observation-error law and sigma definitions, or explicitly unresolved residual structure for a proposed rather than fitted model.
Phoenix Stdev/Mult Stdev/Mix Ratio names and engine settings only if those particular software options are used.
limitations: Phoenix NLME log-additive implementation truncates non-positive values to 0.25 * min(positive_obs), which is a software behavior, not a general data cleaning rule.
Do not force lognormal errors for latent scenarios where observation error is irrelevant.
Parameter identifiability may be compromised if the error model is misspecified relative to the data scale.
downstream_use: Used to define the likelihood function for parameter estimation and to simulate realistic observation data for model validation (VPC) or trial simulation.
retrieval_keywords: residual error model additive multiplicative log-additive combined variance Phoenix NLME Mix Ratio Add+Mult

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Let mu=f(theta,eta) denote a latent prediction. Define one conditional observation model Y|mu with declared error scale and parameters; do not insert the same residual epsilon inside f and add it again. Cover source-established Phoenix combined/log-additive parameterizations without treating one as a universal fit recommendation.
method_recipe.input_contract: Supply observed value and latent mu on the same endpoint/matrix scale, assay/censoring status, concentration range, and candidate sigma definitions. For Phoenix options identify whether eps has additive Stdev sigma_a and whether fixed effect r is Mix Ratio or multStdev is Add+Mult. Do not require residual sigma for a latent-only scenario.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Positive predictions/observations are required for the cited log-additive transform. Other residual forms require a justified distribution and support appropriate to the endpoint. A measured BQL observation contributes censor likelihood/bounds under a qualified method; do not create a positive replacement as policy. Diagnosing a model's structural fit and assay limitations precedes changing the residual law.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: mu and Y share the observed endpoint unit. Additive sigma_a has that unit. Proportional sigma_p or multStdev is dimensionless. Phoenix Mix Ratio r=sigma_mult/sigma_add has inverse endpoint units. Log-additive sigma_log is dimensionless on log(Y). Conditional SD/variance must be stated on the scale used for inference.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Define latent mu=f(theta,eta), observed endpoint, assay range and censor status. 2. Compare justified additive, proportional-normal, log-additive or combined observation structures against assay and diagnostic evidence; do not default by PK versus PD label. 3. For Phoenix, retain its exact Mix Ratio or Add+Mult formula and report sigma meaning; verify whether its log-additive engine actually fits in log space. 4. Evaluate residuals/likelihood on the fitted scale and observed-scale predictive checks separately. 5. For BQL observations preserve the limit and use a separately qualified censor-aware likelihood or bounded result; never treat Phoenix internal nonpositive replacement as scientific imputation.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: Additive normal: Y=mu+eps_a, eps_a~N(0,sigma_a^2), SD(Y|mu)=sigma_a. Proportional normal: Y=mu*(1+eps_p), eps_p~N(0,sigma_p^2), SD=|mu|*sigma_p. Log-additive/lognormal: Y=mu*exp(eps_log), eps_log~N(0,sigma_log^2), so log(Y)=log(mu)+eps_log for positive values and original-scale CV=sqrt(exp(sigma_log^2)-1). Phoenix Mix Ratio: Y=mu+eps*(1+mu*r), eps~N(0,sigma_a^2), r=sigma_mult/sigma_a; Var(Y|mu)=sigma_a^2*(1+mu*r)^2. Phoenix Add+Mult: Y=mu+eps*sqrt(1+(mu*multStdev/sigma_a)^2), eps~N(0,sigma_a^2), multStdev=sigma_mult; Var(Y|mu)=sigma_a^2+(mu*sigma_mult)^2. Mix Ratio and Add+Mult are not the same conditional variance law.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Residual sigma is observation variation conditional on latent parameters, distinct from between-subject variability and parameter uncertainty. Log-additive normal error implies positive lognormal observed values; on the original scale CV=sqrt(exp(sigma_log^2)-1). Combined components may be weakly distinguished over a narrow measurement range; diagnose rather than imposing a fixed form.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: Inspect residuals on their fitted scale and simulate back to the observation scale; systematic trend, heteroscedasticity or low-concentration bias may arise from structure, assay censoring or error law. Do not automatically switch to multiplicative/log-additive or simplify on optimization failure without investigating. Phoenix's nonpositive replacement in log-additive mode is implementation behavior, not a user data-cleaning rule.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If assay precision or observation-error form is unknown, mark the fitted likelihood choice unresolved, compare justified sensitivity alternatives when data permit, and keep latent simulations distinct from observed-value predictions. Preserve BQL limits and refer detailed M2/M3/M4 likelihood to the separate censoring method card.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Report observation equation, error distribution, sigma/ratio definitions and units, estimation scale, conditional observed-scale SD/variance, censor handling and diagnostics. A latent population exposure band does not require residual sigma; an observed-value interval does.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic at mu=10 ng/mL, sigma_a=2 ng/mL, sigma_mult=0.1 and r=0.05 mL/ng: Phoenix Mix Ratio has SD=2*(1+10*0.05)=3 ng/mL and variance=9 (ng/mL)^2. Phoenix Add+Mult has SD=sqrt(2^2+(10*0.1)^2)=sqrt(5)=2.236 ng/mL and variance=5 (ng/mL)^2. These are different models. If sigma_log=0.1, original-scale CV=sqrt(exp(0.01)-1)=0.10025, approximately 10.0%. A single 0/BLQ observation cannot be made valid for log fitting by silently replacing it with 0.25 times the smallest positive value.

claim_support.claim: Phoenix additive, multiplicative and power options imply different observation-scale error magnitudes; its preferences are software guidance.
Phoenix log-additive transforms to log scale only under specified engine conditions; nonpositive replacement is documented software behavior.
claim_support.scope: Phoenix NLME implementation, not data-cleaning policy

claim_support.claim: Mix Ratio r is sigma_mult/sigma_add and has the Phoenix form C+eps*(1+C*r).
Add+Mult uses multStdev as multiplicative sigma and a square-root form with variance sigma_add^2+(C*sigma_mult)^2.
BQL observations may be modeled as censor events rather than set to a fixed fraction of LOQ; detailed methods are a separate branch.

title: Conditional Renal Clearance from Matched Urinary Ae and Plasma AUC
claim: Renal clearance (CLR) is a secondary parameter calculated by dividing the amount of unchanged drug excreted in urine (Ae) over a specific interval by the plasma AUC over the exact same interval. This calculation requires strict matching of subject, analyte, and time window between the urine collection and plasma profile. Low urinary recovery alone does not prove negligible renal elimination; interpretation must consider collection completeness, bioavailability, and nonrenal pathways.
conditions: Conditional on a qualified urine unchanged-analyte amount Ae and plasma AUC for the same subject, analyte and time window; sampling instants need not coincide with collection boundaries if the AUC method supports the window.
Urine volume/collection and analyte stability are adequately documented for the chosen interval.
Not a universal measurement requirement for every compound or route.
required_inputs: Urinary amount excreted (Ae) for the unchanged drug (parent or specific metabolite).
Plasma concentration-time data sufficient to calculate AUC over the same interval as the urine collection.
Matching subject IDs and analyte identifiers between urine and plasma datasets.
Explicit time intervals (start/end) for both urine collection and plasma AUC calculation.
limitations: Do not use Ae/AUC computed over mismatched intervals.
Do not treat low urine recovery alone as proof of negligible renal elimination without considering collection duration/completeness, bioavailability/route, analyte stability, and nonrenal pathways.
Parent and metabolite analytes must be kept separate; do not mix analytes in the ratio.
downstream_use: Use to estimate renal clearance for specific intervals when paired urine and plasma data exist. Propagate exclusions from plasma AUC or urine Ae to the CLR output. Do not substitute allometry or assume negligible renal elimination based solely on low recovery.
retrieval_keywords: renal clearance calculation, Ae over AUC, matched interval PK, secondary parameter linkage, urine plasma matching, CLR interval, analyte specific clearance

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Estimate renal clearance (CLR) for a specific analyte over a specific time interval by linking urinary excretion data to plasma exposure data. Scope is limited to intervals where both urine Ae and plasma AUC are available and matched.
method_recipe.input_contract: Urine: subject, analyte, interval start/end, collection volume/completeness and unchanged-analyte Ae with units. Plasma: same subject/analyte with concentration-time records sufficient to calculate AUC over that identical interval. The AUC interval boundary is a computation definition, not a requirement that a blood sample occur exactly at each urine boundary.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: The same-subject, same-analyte plasma profile must support an AUC for precisely the Ae collection interval using a stated interpolation/extrapolation rule. Propagate any reference-AUC exclusion to CLR. A potentially incomplete urine collection or analyte loss remains an uncertainty/qualification issue, not an automatic zero CLR.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: CLR_interval = Ae_unchanged,interval / AUC_plasma,same_interval. Units: Ae in mass (e.g., mg), AUC in concentration*time (e.g., mg*h/L), resulting CLR in volume/time (e.g., L/h). Basis: Mass balance over the interval. Window: Must be identical for numerator and denominator.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Identify urine records with Ae for the target analyte and interval [t_start, t_end]. 2. Identify plasma records for the same subject and analyte covering [t_start, t_end]. 3. Calculate AUC_plasma over [t_start, t_end] using the specified method (e.g., linear). 4. Link the urine Ae to the plasma AUC using the matching subject, analyte, and interval. 5. Compute CLR = Ae / AUC. 6. If the plasma AUC is excluded (e.g., due to too few points), mark the CLR as excluded with the same reason. 7. Ensure parent and metabolite CLR calculations are kept separate.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: CLR = Ae / AUC. In PKNCA, this is handled as a secondary parameter where the urine interval links to a plasma reference interval. The 'group_ref' or automatic reference derivation must ensure the plasma profile matches the analyte of the urine sample.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Ae uncertainty includes collection completeness and analyte stability; AUC uncertainty includes sampling, interpolation and any extrapolation. Unrecovered unchanged analyte can make Ae and CLR spuriously low if other errors are absent, but the net direction is conditional on collection and assay errors. The supplied vignette does not give a universal CLR confidence-interval propagation method.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: Failure: Mismatched intervals, mismatched analytes, or missing plasma data for the interval. Diagnostic: Check if the reference interval was automatically derived correctly. Check if exclusions on plasma AUC propagated to CLR. Failure Mode: If plasma AUC is NA due to insufficient points, CLR must be NA.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If matched interval AUC cannot be computed, CLR is unavailable (not zero or allometrically replaced). If collection completeness/stability is unknown, retain Ae/AUC as a qualified conditional estimate or flag it unresolved rather than asserting a universal downward bias. Keep parent and metabolite analytes distinct.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Report CLR=Ae_unchanged/AUC_plasma for the declared analyte/window in volume/time, link IDs, collection/AUC provenance and uncertainty qualifiers. A low CLR is not by itself a fraction-of-dose or nonrenal-mechanism conclusion; consider duration/completeness, binding, route/F and competing clearance pathways.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Example: Subject 1, Parent analyte. Urine Ae (0-24h) = 350 mg. Plasma AUC (0-24h) = 144 mg*h/L. CLR = 350 / 144 = 2.43 L/h. Counterexample: If Plasma AUC (0-24h) is excluded due to 'too few points', CLR is NA, not 0 or estimated.

claim_support.claim: Renal clearance is a secondary parameter linking urine Ae to plasma AUC over the same interval.
claim_support.scope: General PK analysis with paired urine/plasma data.

claim_support.claim: Calculation requires matching subject, analyte, and interval; exclusions on AUC propagate to CLR.
Parent and metabolite analytes must be kept separate in CLR calculations.
Arithmetic demonstration: 350/144 = 2.430556 in consistent units.

title: Source-Case Susceptible/Resting Time-Kill Hypothesis and Data Contract (Non-Executable)
claim: The SUP006 in-vitro source model describes growing susceptible S and resting R populations, total B=S+R, density-related S-to-R transfer and drug effect applied to S. It explored first-order drug degradation and effect delay; kRS=0 was a source-case constant-pressure/no-dilution assumption. The exact equation tables e1-e7 are image-only in the present library, so this card is a non-executable structural hypothesis and data contract, not a fitted dynamic method or target-drug mechanism claim.
conditions: Applicable only when an in-vitro time-kill question warrants comparing a susceptible/resting hypothesis with simpler explanations; this model is not a required generic time-kill analysis.
SUP006's constant-pressure/no-dilution setup, kRS=0, first-order degradation, effect delay and latent mixtures are source-case assumptions or optional candidates, not transferable defaults.
An executable S/R model requires visual verification and hash-bound transcription of original equation images e1-e7, plus identifiability and data checks.
required_inputs: Observed CFU-versus-time and actual exposure/dosing schedule, with organism, assay count limit and replicate/experimental-unit provenance.
Drug stability/concentration measurements when the objective is to test depletion as a regrowth explanation; otherwise retain mechanism uncertainty.

For any executable S/R fit: visually verified source equations, declared initial-state assumptions and data informative for model parameters. Initial resting fraction and mixture parameters may be fitted or scenario assumptions rather than observed raw inputs.
limitations: Exact SUP006 e1-e7 equations are image-only in the current source packet; do not state or fit specific ODEs until verified transcription is added.
kRS=0, first-order degradation, delayed effect, NONMEM implementation, latent mixture and the paper's LOD/2-first/omit-later rule are source choices, not universal prerequisites or cleaning rules.
Curve shape/regrowth alone cannot identify persistence, resistance, depletion or R-to-S transfer; no target-drug dynamic parameters are supplied.
downstream_use: Use only as a source-case S/R hypothesis and data/provenance checklist alongside the existing general B03 time-kill design card. The equation-image gap blocks executable dynamic modeling until a verified transcription and model qualification are supplied.
retrieval_keywords: time-kill PK/PD model susceptible resting compartments effect delay drug degradation density-dependent transfer NONMEM censoring replicate structure

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Non-executable companion to the general time-kill design/interpretation card: specify observed longitudinal CFU, censor/replicate status and competing S/R versus simpler mechanistic hypotheses. No numerical S/R state-parameter estimand is available from the present image-only equations.
method_recipe.input_contract: Observed times and viable counts (including <LOD status), experimental run/specimen/replicate identifiers, organism and exposure schedule. Stability measurements and initial-state information are conditional on the hypothesis to be tested. Verified e1-e7 equations are mandatory only for executable S/R fitting.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Use for a qualified in-vitro time-kill design where a source-case S/R interpretation is under consideration. The existing B03 card covers generic curve design; this companion only adds the source's latent S/R structural hypothesis and equation-extraction gate. Do not use source-specific culture conditions as universal criteria.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: S is the source's growing susceptible subpopulation, R its resting subpopulation, and B=S+R is total viable burden in CFU/mL. k_growth, k_death, kSR/kRS, Bmax, drug degradation and effect-delay terms are source model concepts, not estimable definitions without verified equations and chosen parameterization. The source fixed kRS=0 in its constant-pressure/no-dilution experiments only.
method_recipe.procedure: 1. Preserve observed CFU/time, count limit/censor flags, run/replicate lineage and exposure/stability information; do not apply LOD/2 or drop records by default. 2. Plot/describe early kill, stationary behavior and regrowth on their measured windows; compare untreated controls and exposure history where available. 3. Record source-case S/R graph in words: S growing/susceptible, R resting, B=S+R, density-linked S-to-R transfer, drug effect on S. Treat kRS=0, degradation, effect delay and latent inoculum mixtures as alternative assumptions to test, not defaults. 4. List competing explanations and what additional observations could distinguish them. 5. Stop before numerical S/R ODE fitting until M1.gif-M7.gif are visually verified, transcribed with source hash and model/data identifiability assessed.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: Text-supported identity only: B=S+R. The exact SUP006 equations e1-e7 (including dS/dt, dR/dt, concentration/effect dynamics and parameterization of transfer/drug action) are present only as image links in the original HTML and are not verified text chunks. No executable differential equation is supplied by this card.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Initial inoculum composition, degradation, effect delay and replicate/run variability can be uncertain. SUP006 explored a mixture model and a split residual structure for its experiments, but these are optional source-case mechanisms. Without exact equations and informative data, S/R parameters cannot be claimed identifiable or numerically estimated.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: Observed regrowth can arise under multiple exposure and bacterial-state mechanisms; it does not by itself falsify the paper's kRS=0 assumption or prove genetic resistance/persistence. If drug stability was not measured, depletion remains unresolved. If CFU is below the assay limit, keep censor status and avoid treating it as zero. A misleading exact ODE transcription is a stop condition for executable modeling.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: If equation images are not yet visually verified, retain descriptive time-kill and explicit S/R hypothesis only; do not substitute a fabricated one-compartment/direct-Emax fit. If stability data are unavailable, do not assume constant exposure; label drug-loss contribution unresolved. Missing target-drug parameters do not invalidate descriptive plots.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Output an observed/censored time-kill summary, provenance, optional source-case S/R model graph, competing hypotheses and equation/data gaps. Do not output fitted k_growth, k_death, Bmax, kdeg, ke, Emax, EC50, gamma or mixture fractions until an executable, verified and identifiable model exists.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: Synthetic descriptive example: CFU begins at 10^6/mL, is reported <10^3/mL at 6 h and is quantified at 10^5/mL at 12 h. Early reduction exceeds 3 log10 and later regrowth relative to the <10^3 bound exceeds 2 log10; the exact 6-h count and cause of regrowth remain unknown. Neither this shape nor kRS=0 alone establishes a specific S/R transfer rate, resistance or persistence.

claim_support.claim: The source-case bacterial system has growing susceptible S, resting R, B=S+R, density-related S-to-R transfer and kRS=0 under its experimental assumptions.
The paper explored first-order drug degradation/effect delay and applied drug effect to susceptible bacteria; exact equation tables are absent from extracted text.
claim_support.scope: SUP006 source-case hypotheses and extraction limit

claim_support.claim: The paper used a historical LOD/2-first/omit-later rule and mixture/run error model; those are examples, not general policies.
Time-kill kinetics alone can be insufficient for unique resistance-mechanism inference.
